talks.session_title: Opening Welcome Remarks
talks.title: CoRL 2026 Opening Remarks
talks.summary: The opening ceremony of CoRL 2026 provides an overview of the conference's growth, the rigorous review process, and the diverse program including keynotes, workshops, and live demos. Local organizers also share logistical information and highlight the robotics research ecosystem at UT Austin.
talks.official_abstract: As foundation models expand what robots can already do, an equally important question is how to expand their learning potential: learning reusable action spaces for safe physical exploration, using human demonstrations and corrections for real-world refinement, and selecting experience according to policy improvement.
talks.speaker_bio: Roberto Martín-Martín is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at UT Austin, where he directs the Robot Interactive Intelligence Lab (RobIn). He earned his Ph.D. at TU Berlin and was a postdoc at Stanford SVL.

subsections.title: Welcome and Conference History
subsections.visual_caption: Timeline of CoRL conferences and host cities.
subsections.summary: Yuke Zhu welcomes attendees to Austin and reflects on the growth of CoRL since its inception in 2017.

subsections.title: Conference Growth and Logistics
subsections.visual_caption: Statistics on conference attendance and paper submissions.
subsections.summary: Overview of the record-breaking attendance and submission numbers, and introduction of the multi-venue format.

subsections.title: Paper Statistics and Review Process
subsections.visual_caption: CoRL 2026 Paper Statistics
subsections.summary: Organizers discuss the record-breaking 2,084 submissions, the 32.8% acceptance rate, and the new hierarchical review team structure involving Senior Area Chairs to manage the scale.

subsections.title: Program Highlights and Keynotes
subsections.visual_caption: Keynotes and Fireside Chat Schedule
subsections.summary: An overview of the three-day program, featuring early career keynotes, main keynotes from Wolfram Burgard, Russ Tedrake, and Fei-Fei Li, and a fireside chat with Lisa Su.

subsections.title: Workshops and Live Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Workshops and Tutorials Overview
subsections.summary: Workshop chairs highlight the 32 accepted workshops and 17 live robot demos scheduled across multiple venues to encourage interaction.

subsections.title: Local Logistics and Inclusion
subsections.visual_caption: Getting Around Austin Map
subsections.summary: Logistics regarding venues (Hilton and JW Marriott), Wi-Fi, transportation, and inclusion initiatives like childcare and travel grants are presented.

subsections.title: Texas Robotics and School of Computing
subsections.visual_caption: The Historic Anna Hiss Gymnasium
subsections.summary: Peter Stone introduces the Texas Robotics consortium and the new School of Computing at UT Austin, highlighting state-of-the-art facilities and massive faculty hiring plans.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: MolmoAct2: Action Reasoning Models for Real-World Deployment
talks.summary: MolmoAct2 is an open-science robotics foundation model that bridges visual understanding and action generation through explicit embodied reasoning. The work provides an open recipe for pre-training, mid-training, and adaptation, demonstrating zero-shot deployment capabilities across diverse real-world tasks.

subsections.title: The Need for Open Foundation Models
subsections.visual_caption: Robots Deployed Today vs. New Autonomy
subsections.summary: The speaker argues for open-source robotics foundation models to overcome the limitations of custom-built, expert-programmed systems and promote reproducibility.

subsections.title: MolmoAct2 Architecture and Reasoning
subsections.visual_caption: MolmoAct2 Training Pipeline
subsections.summary: Introduction of the 'Think-Act' paradigm where the model performs explicit spatial reasoning (e.g., depth perception) as an intermediate step before generating actions.

subsections.title: Evaluation and Real-World Deployment
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world Evaluation Results
subsections.summary: The model's performance is validated through blind third-party evaluations and zero-shot deployment on various robot platforms, showing strong generalization.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: Semantic Anchoring for Robotic Action Representations
talks.summary: This work addresses the problem of representation degradation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models during downstream fine-tuning. The authors propose 'semantic anchoring,' a method that aligns action representations with frozen vision-language embeddings to preserve generalization capabilities.

subsections.title: Motivation: Representation Degradation
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of task-level clusters showing degradation after vanilla fine-tuning.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains how fine-tuning on narrow data can erode the high-quality representations inherited from pre-trained models, leading to poor generalization.

subsections.title: Method: Semantic Anchoring
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the Semantic Anchoring architecture splitting features into shared and private parts.
subsections.summary: The proposed method splits features into a shared semantic representation aligned with a frozen VL encoder and a private representation for execution-specific details.

subsections.title: Results: Simulation and Real-Robot
subsections.visual_caption: Real-robot experiment results comparing the proposed method against baselines.
subsections.summary: The method shows consistent improvements across multiple VLA architectures in both simulation and real-world robot experiments, particularly in out-of-distribution tasks.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: MEM: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory for Vision Language Action Models
talks.summary: MEM introduces a multi-scale memory architecture for VLAs to solve long-horizon tasks that require memory of past events. By combining short-term visual memory with long-term textual summaries, the model can handle tasks lasting up to 15 minutes.

subsections.title: Problem: Memory in VLAs
subsections.visual_caption: Analysis showing how raw video memory quickly exceeds token limits for long tasks.
subsections.summary: The speaker demonstrates that current VLA policies lack memory, leading to repetitive failures, and explains why simply adding raw video frames to the context is computationally infeasible.

subsections.title: Method: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram of MEM showing the low-level and high-level VLA loops.
subsections.summary: MEM decomposes memory into short-term visual frames and long-term textual summaries, which are fed back into the VLA recursively.

subsections.title: Results: Long-Horizon Kitchen Tasks
subsections.visual_caption: Robot demo showing in-context adaptation after a failed attempt to open a drawer.
subsections.summary: The system successfully completes complex kitchen tasks and demonstrates in-context adaptation, changing strategies on the fly after a failed attempt.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: PRTS: A Primitive Reasoning and Tasking System via Contrastive Representations
talks.summary: PRTS is a VLA foundation model that integrates language-conditioned contrastive reinforcement learning (CRL) into large-scale pre-training. This approach allows the model to capture goal reachability and temporal progress from demonstrations without extra reward labels.

subsections.title: Motivation: Goal Reachability
subsections.visual_caption: Illustration of a robot making progress toward an instruction goal.
subsections.summary: The speaker argues that standard behavior cloning fails to capture how much progress an action makes toward a goal, necessitating a goal-reachability objective.

subsections.title: Method: Language-Conditioned Contrastive RL
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the PRTS pre-training architecture with the CRL objective.
subsections.summary: The method uses contrastive learning to align state-action pairs with language goals, using temporal weighting to emphasize moments closer to completion.

subsections.title: Real-World Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Grid of real-world robot manipulation demos using PRTS.
subsections.summary: PRTS is scaled to 400 million samples and demonstrates robustness to human intervention and zero-shot generalization to novel objects in the real world.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: Learning What to Say to Your VLA: Mostly Harmless Vision Language Action Model Steering
talks.summary: This work introduces a language feedback policy (LFP) to 'steer' pre-trained VLAs by interactively searching for local language instructions that elicit the desired behavior. This approach avoids the need for expensive fine-tuning while improving performance on brittle tasks.

subsections.title: Problem: Brittle Language-to-Action Mapping
subsections.visual_caption: Robot demo showing how different task instructions lead to different success outcomes.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights that VLAs can be brittle to specific language instructions, often failing even when they possess the underlying motor skills.

subsections.title: Method: Language Feedback Policy
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the LFP calibration using class-conditional conformal prediction.
subsections.summary: The LFP interactively searches the local language space for perturbations that improve performance, using conformal prediction to ensure the steering does no harm.

subsections.title: Results: Steering Success
subsections.visual_caption: Bar charts showing success rate improvements across different VLA models.
subsections.summary: The method significantly improves success rates for models like pi-0.5 and MolmoAct2 in both simulation and hardware environments.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs
talks.affiliation: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
talks.summary: This research identifies 'counterfactual failures' in VLAs, where models ignore language instructions in favor of well-learned visual shortcuts. The authors introduce the LIBERO-CF benchmark and a training-free mitigation method called Counterfactual Action Guidance (CAG).

subsections.title: Motivation: Counterfactual Failures
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of a robot correctly following an instruction vs. repeating a learned shortcut.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains how modality imbalance leads VLAs to rely too heavily on visual cues, causing them to repeat training tasks even when instructed otherwise.

subsections.title: Benchmark: LIBERO-CF
subsections.visual_caption: Table showing high performance of VLAs even when language is removed, indicating vision shortcuts.
subsections.summary: LIBERO-CF is introduced as a benchmark with 50 counterfactual tasks to systematically evaluate language-following abilities.

subsections.title: Method: Counterfactual Action Guidance
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world experiment results showing CAG correcting counterfactual failures.
subsections.summary: CAG is a dual-branch inference scheme that amplifies language-induced action differences, effectively reducing vision bias without requiring new training data.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: ZETA: A Controlled Study of Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment VLA Transfer for Tabletop Manipulation
talks.summary: ZETA provides a controlled study of zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer for VLAs. The authors investigate what drives successful transfer to new robot bodies and find that local end-effector-centered representations and source robot diversity are critical factors.

subsections.title: Defining Zero-Shot Transfer
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of 'Strict' vs. 'Pretrain-Exposed' zero-shot transfer definitions.
subsections.summary: The speaker clarifies the meaning of zero-shot transfer, distinguishing between cases where the target robot was never seen versus seen only during pre-training.

subsections.title: Controlled Benchmark and Research Questions
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of the 14 unseen target robot variants used in the study.
subsections.summary: The study uses a benchmark where only the robot changes, testing four research questions regarding representation, source diversity, auxiliary training, and target exposure.

subsections.title: Key Takeaways
subsections.visual_caption: Summary slide of the four research question findings.
subsections.summary: The findings suggest favoring local representations, balancing source diversity with data budget, and explicitly reporting target exposure levels.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: EmbodiSteer: Steering Embodiment-Agnostic Visuomotor Policies with Joint-Space Guidance for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Deployment
talks.summary: EmbodiSteer addresses the challenge of deploying embodiment-agnostic policies on different robot arms. It uses a two-step process involving joint-space sampling and task-aware guidance to ensure collision-free execution while preserving the original policy's task performance.

subsections.title: Motivation: Action Space Tradeoffs
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison showing a Cartesian policy causing a robot arm collision.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains the tradeoff between Cartesian actions (easy to share but body-unaware) and joint actions (body-aware but robot-specific).

subsections.title: Method: Joint-Space Sampling and Guidance
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of the whole-body guidance with task preservation.
subsections.summary: EmbodiSteer separates learning from execution, using a frozen Cartesian policy to guide joint-space sampling and optimization for clearance.

subsections.title: Results: Zero-Shot Deployment
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world results comparing EmbodiSteer against base policies on UR5 and Panda robots.
subsections.summary: The method significantly increases success rates and reduces collisions across different robot arms without requiring robot-specific training.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S1: Generalist policies, memory and transfer
talks.title: Diagnosing Compositional Generalization in Sequential Robot Tasks
talks.summary: This work diagnoses why robot policies often fail on unfamiliar combinations of subtasks in sequential settings. The authors find that failures are primarily due to 'instruction steering' issues rather than a lack of underlying skills, and that full task enumeration is unnecessary for generalization.

subsections.title: Problem: Sparse Sequential Data
subsections.visual_caption: Analysis showing performance saturation with only a fraction of task combinations.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains how the number of possible sequential tasks grows exponentially, making real datasets sparse and leading to failures in unfamiliar combinations.

subsections.title: Analysis: Instruction Steering vs. Skills
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing how subtasks depend on each other in a two-stage task.
subsections.summary: The research shows that skills are reusable across tasks, but the policy struggles to follow instructions when subtasks have complex dependencies.

subsections.title: Takeaways
subsections.visual_caption: Summary slide of the three key takeaways from the study.
subsections.summary: Key findings include that full enumeration is unnecessary, sparse failures are steering problems, and dependent tasks require relational coverage.

talks.session_title: Early Career Keynote I — Hang Zhao
talks.title: Organizing Physical AI Across Timescales
talks.summary: Hang Zhao discusses the organization of physical AI systems across different timescales, proposing a hierarchical architecture (System 0, 1, and 2) based on reaction speeds rather than just functions. He presents several works from his lab, including Fast-WAM, ActionCodec2, and whole-body control models, emphasizing the need for fast reflexes and effective feedback loops between layers.
talks.official_abstract: The physical world does not pause while a robot computes. Frontier models can now drive robots, yet they take seconds to choose a motion while contact unfolds in milliseconds. Rather than dividing a robot's intelligence by function, this talk argues for dividing it by timescale, from S2 reasoning over seconds, through S1 policies at tens of hertz, to S0 control at hundreds of hertz, with each layer still learned end to end.
talks.speaker_bio: Hang Zhao is an Assistant Professor at IIIS, Tsinghua University, and a co-founder of Galaxea AI. Before joining Tsinghua, he was a research scientist at Waymo. He received his Ph.D. from MIT, advised by Antonio Torralba.

subsections.title: Introduction and Research Journey
subsections.visual_caption: Slide summarizing Hang Zhao's research journey from wheels to legs to arms.
subsections.summary: The speaker is introduced and shares his background in self-driving cars and legged locomotion before transitioning to robot manipulation.

subsections.title: Frontier Models vs. Robot Models
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison table of GPT-6 Astra vs. pi-0.5 on simulation benchmarks.
subsections.summary: Zhao discusses how recent frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are beginning to rival specialized robot models in task success on simulation benchmarks.

subsections.title: The Problem of Thinking Time
subsections.visual_caption: Analysis showing a robot spending 97% of its time waiting for a model to 'think'.
subsections.summary: A critical bottleneck is identified: large foundation models take significant time to process, leaving robots idle and unable to react to fast physical changes.

subsections.title: Benchmarks and the Latency Problem
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of success rates for different model calling policies with and without a real-time clock.
subsections.summary: Zhao highlights that current robotics benchmarks often ignore model inference time, showing that step-by-step policies that work in simulation often fail on real robots due to latency.

subsections.title: Hierarchical System Design by Clock Speed
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the proposed hierarchy: System 2 (seconds), System 1 (tens of Hz), and System 0 (hundreds of Hz).
subsections.summary: The speaker proposes a new way to split robotic systems based on their required reaction frequency, defining System 2 for high-level planning, System 1 for reactive skills, and System 0 for low-level control.

subsections.title: Accelerating System 1: Fast-WAM and ActionCodec2
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture of Fast-WAM, showing how it trains with video but acts without it to reduce latency.
subsections.summary: Zhao presents methods to make System 1 faster, including Fast-WAM which skips expensive video generation during inference and ActionCodec2 which uses a streaming tokenizer for continuous action execution.

subsections.title: Inter-layer Communication: Intent and Force
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing the flow of intent downwards and feedback upwards between the hierarchical systems.
subsections.summary: This section explores the interface between systems, arguing that communication should include not just motion commands but also intent, contact information, and force feedback to handle complex interactions.

subsections.title: Future Outlook and Takeaways
subsections.visual_caption: Summary slide listing the importance of clock-based design, interfaces, and multi-clock system design.
subsections.summary: Zhao concludes by outlining two potential paths for future research: layered loops with explicit feedback or unified models with internal multi-clock experts, stressing that the clock must be part of the design.

subsections.title: Q&A: Compute Allocation and Sensing Latency
subsections.visual_caption: Hang Zhao answering questions from the audience at the podium.
subsections.summary: Zhao answers questions regarding the physical location of compute (cloud vs. edge) for different layers and the necessary sensing latencies for modalities like touch versus vision.

talks.session_title: Oral O1: Generalist policies and context scaling
talks.title: π 0.7 : a Steerable Generalist Robotic Foundation Model with Emergent Capabilities
talks.summary: The authors present π 0.7, a steerable generalist robotic foundation model. By leveraging detailed metadata prompting, the model can fit highly diverse, mixed-quality data and exhibits emergent compositional generalization, such as cross-embodiment transfer.

subsections.title: Motivation: Generalists vs Specialists
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing how generalists can compose concepts, unlike narrow specialists.
subsections.summary: The speakers introduce the limitations of specialist robot policies and the promise of generalist models that can compose learned abilities to handle new tasks.

subsections.title: Detailed Metadata Prompting
subsections.visual_caption: Slide detailing prompt expansion for robot control, including subgoals, instructions, and metadata.
subsections.summary: To fit diverse and dexterous data, the authors borrow from digital foundation models by using detailed multimodal prompts that specify not just what to do, but how to do it.

subsections.title: Generalist Performance & Mixed Quality Data
subsections.visual_caption: Bar charts showing detailed metadata prompting enables fitting diverse data and learning from mixed quality data.
subsections.summary: The generalist model matches or exceeds prior specialist models. Metadata prompting also allows the model to learn effectively from mixed-quality data by conditioning on behavior quality.

subsections.title: Emergent Compositional Generalization
subsections.visual_caption: Slide demonstrating cross-embodiment generalization, combining folding knowledge with a new robot arm.
subsections.summary: The model demonstrates emergent capabilities, such as cross-embodiment transfer, where it combines task knowledge (e.g., folding) with control knowledge of a different robot arm to perform the task autonomously.

subsections.title: Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Speakers answering audience questions.
subsections.summary: The speakers address questions regarding how high-quality data is selected and the iterative process of defining metadata quality metrics.

talks.session_title: Oral O1: Generalist policies and context scaling
talks.title: Being-H0.5: Scaling Human-Centric Robot Learning for Cross-Embodiment Generalization
talks.affiliation: Peking University, BeingBeyond, Renmin University of China, Tsinghua University
talks.summary: This paper introduces Being-H0.5, a human-centric robot learning framework that leverages abundant human video data to learn a shared prior, which is then specialized for diverse robot embodiments to achieve cross-embodiment generalization.

subsections.title: Motivation & Human-Centric Learning
subsections.visual_caption: Slide explaining why human-centric learning addresses robot data scarcity and imbalance.
subsections.summary: The presenter explains the challenges of data scarcity and imbalance across different robot embodiments, proposing human data as a universal, abundant anchor to bridge these gaps.

subsections.title: Pre-training Corpus & Unified Action Space
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the unified action space and sequence modeling architecture.
subsections.summary: The method uses a shared human-centric corpus and a unified action space where human and robot actions share slots, allowing the model to learn a shared prior through sequence modeling.

subsections.title: Embodiment Specialization
subsections.visual_caption: Slide detailing embodiment specialization via dynamics, observation shift, and control timing.
subsections.summary: To adapt the shared prior to specific robots, the model employs a mixture-of-flow architecture for dynamics, manifold-preserving gating for observation shifts, and universal async chunking for control timing.

subsections.title: Real-World Evaluation
subsections.visual_caption: Results showing the generalist checkpoint performing across five embodiments.
subsections.summary: Evaluations show that a single generalist checkpoint can serve multiple embodiments effectively, demonstrating positive co-training transfer and robustness to unseen tasks and environment shifts.

subsections.title: Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Presenter answering a question about human action labels.
subsections.summary: The presenter clarifies how human hand motion labels are extracted from open-source videos using reconstruction pipelines and heuristic filtering.

talks.session_title: Oral O1: Generalist policies and context scaling
talks.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
talks.summary: RoboTTT scales the context window for robot policies up to 8,000 timesteps using Test-Time Training (TTT) layers integrated into a Diffusion Transformer (DiT). This enables in-context learning, on-the-fly failure correction, and long-horizon task tracking.

subsections.title: Motivation & Test-Time Training
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram explaining Test-Time Training (TTT) as sequence modeling with fast weights.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights the gap in context scaling between LLMs and robot policies, introducing Test-Time Training (TTT) as a mechanism to maintain a recurrent state via fast weights updated by gradient descent.

subsections.title: RoboTTT Architecture & Sequence Action Forcing
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram showing TTT layers added to a DiT block.
subsections.summary: RoboTTT integrates TTT layers into a pre-trained DiT model. To handle the temporal correlation of robot trajectories, the authors introduce sequence action forcing, applying different noise levels per action chunk.

subsections.title: Effective Learning from Context
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing how fast-weight updates are decoupled for conditioning and imitation targets.
subsections.summary: The method decouples fast-weight updates, using masked timesteps for pure context conditioning and unmasked timesteps as imitation targets, enabling capabilities like one-shot imitation and failure correction.

subsections.title: Experiments & Robot Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Video of the robot autonomously assembling a gear bot.
subsections.summary: RoboTTT is evaluated on long-horizon bimanual assembly tasks, significantly outperforming baselines and demonstrating the ability to complete complex, multi-stage assemblies.

subsections.title: Context Length Scaling & Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Graph showing task completion score increasing with longer context lengths.
subsections.summary: The results show clear performance gains as context length scales from 128 to 8,000 timesteps. The session concludes with a Q&A on the use of human data for context prompting.

talks.session_title: Oral O2: World models and temporal representations
talks.title: World Action Models are Zero-shot Policies
talks.summary: This talk introduces DreamZero, a 14B autoregressive World Action Model (WAM) that leverages pre-trained video generation models to perform zero-shot robot manipulation. By fine-tuning the model for joint video-action flow matching, the authors demonstrate that WAMs can effectively generalize to unseen tasks and environments.

subsections.title: Motivation: Humans vs Robots Zero-Shot
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing that video models already know about robot actions.
subsections.summary: The presentation begins by contrasting human zero-shot capabilities with current robot limitations, proposing that video generation models contain the necessary priors for zero-shot robot policies.

subsections.title: DreamZero Architecture and Training
subsections.visual_caption: DreamZero architecture diagram showing joint video-action flow matching.
subsections.summary: The talk details the DreamZero architecture, which adds action and state modalities to a pre-trained video model and uses teacher-forcing for joint video-action denoising.

subsections.title: Experimental Results and Inference Optimization
subsections.visual_caption: Performance comparison chart showing DreamZero outperforming baselines on seen and unseen tasks.
subsections.summary: The authors present experimental results showing DreamZero's superior performance and discuss inference optimizations that achieved a 38x speedup on GB200 GPUs.

talks.session_title: Oral O2: World models and temporal representations
talks.title: Memory-augmented Action-conditioned World Model for Robot Manipulation
talks.affiliation: Dalian University of Technology, Samsung R&D Institute China-Beijing
talks.summary: This talk presents Mem-World, a memory-augmented world model designed to sustain long-horizon robot interactions by addressing visual occlusion and distortion. The model uses a wrist-centered 4D-surfel memory to store and retrieve relevant visual history, significantly improving visual consistency and policy performance.

subsections.title: Motivation: The Problem of Visual Occlusion
subsections.visual_caption: Illustration of how visual occlusion leads to policy failure in standard world models.
subsections.summary: The presenter explains how objects moving out of view or becoming distorted during robot motion causes standard world models to lose context, leading to task failure.

subsections.title: Mem-World Architecture
subsections.visual_caption: Mem-World pipeline diagram showing the wrist-centered 4D-surfel memory module.
subsections.summary: The talk introduces the Mem-World pipeline, which uses a 4D-surfel memory to store visual history and uses future actions as a query to retrieve relevant information.

subsections.title: Experimental Results and Visual Consistency
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of policy performance and visual consistency between Mem-World and baselines.
subsections.summary: The authors demonstrate that Mem-World improves visual consistency and policy success rates on long-horizon tasks by effectively leveraging memory.

talks.session_title: Oral O2: World models and temporal representations
talks.title: TEMPO: Learning Temporal Context for Dynamic Robot Manipulation
talks.summary: This talk introduces TEMPO, a method for learning temporal context to improve dynamic robot manipulation. By incorporating motion cues and action history into a Vision-Language Model (VLM), TEMPO enables robots to anticipate object dynamics and perform complex, fast-paced tasks like catching and handing over objects.

subsections.title: Motivation: Dynamic Tasks and Missing Ingredients
subsections.visual_caption: Examples of dynamic tasks and failure modes in standard VLA policies.
subsections.summary: The presenters highlight the limitations of standard VLA policies in dynamic environments and identify scene dynamics and state disambiguation as missing ingredients.

subsections.title: TEMPO Method: Motion Cues and Action History
subsections.visual_caption: TEMPO architecture diagram showing the integration of motion cues and action history tokens.
subsections.summary: The talk explains how TEMPO integrates motion cues from video foundation models and action history tokens into a VLM to provide necessary temporal context.

subsections.title: Results on Dynamic Manipulation Tasks
subsections.visual_caption: Performance comparison showing TEMPO significantly improving success rates on dynamic tasks.
subsections.summary: The authors present results showing that TEMPO significantly improves success rates on challenging dynamic tasks like bottle handover and ball catching.

talks.session_title: Oral O3: Data, simulation and evaluation
talks.title: Diversity You Can Actually Measure: A Fast, Model-Free Diversity Metric for Robotics Datasets
talks.affiliation: The University of Sydney, University of Toronto, Stanford University, Vector Institute for AI, NVIDIA
talks.summary: This talk introduces Signature Entropy, a principled, non-parametric diversity metric for robotics datasets that depends only on the trajectories themselves. The authors also present FAKTUAL, a fast model-free data curation algorithm that selects diverse subsets of trajectories to improve policy learning efficiency.

subsections.title: Motivation: The Lack of Diversity Metrics
subsections.visual_caption: Bar chart showing the frequency of the word 'diversity' in CoRL 2026 papers vs. the lack of formal definitions.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights that while 'diversity' is frequently mentioned in robotics literature, there is no standard definition or quantitative measure for it in the context of robot datasets.

subsections.title: Signature Entropy and FAKTUAL Algorithm
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the Signature Entropy computation pipeline from trajectories to kernel matrices.
subsections.summary: The method uses signature transforms to map trajectories of varying lengths into a feature vector space, allowing for the computation of a kernel matrix and subsequent Shannon entropy to measure diversity.

subsections.title: Experimental Results and Policy Success
subsections.visual_caption: Plots showing the strong correlation between signature entropy and policy success rate across different benchmarks.
subsections.summary: Results on RoboMimic and real-robot tasks demonstrate that Signature Entropy strongly correlates with policy success and that FAKTUAL-curated subsets can match or beat the performance of full datasets.

subsections.title: Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Speaker answering questions from the audience.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the scalability of the method, noting that computing the diversity score for 1,000 demos takes less than a second on a GPU.

talks.session_title: Oral O3: Data, simulation and evaluation
talks.title: MolmoB0T: Large-Scale Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Manipulation
talks.affiliation: Allen Institute for AI, University of Washington, University of Chicago, TU Darmstadt
talks.summary: MolmoB0T is a family of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models trained exclusively on large-scale synthetic simulation data that transfer zero-shot to real-world robot manipulation. The work introduces MolmoBot-Engine for scalable data generation and MolmoBot-Data, a massive dataset of 1.7 million demonstrations across diverse environments.

subsections.title: MolmoBot-Engine and Data Generation
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of the MolmoBot-Engine pipeline sampling scenes and objects for pick-and-place tasks.
subsections.summary: The authors describe a scalable synthetic data engine that leverages MolmoSpaces to generate millions of diverse robot demonstrations with aggressive randomization of textures, lighting, and camera poses.

subsections.title: MolmoBot-Data and Model Architectures
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison table showing MolmoBot-Data scale vs. other datasets like RoboCasa and Open X-Embodiment.
subsections.summary: MolmoBot-Data contains 1.7 million demonstrations across 94,000 unique environments, significantly exceeding the diversity of existing real-world and simulated datasets.

subsections.title: Real-World Zero-Shot Evaluations
subsections.visual_caption: Real-robot video showing MolmoB0T successfully performing a task despite adversarial table height changes.
subsections.summary: Extensive real-world testing on Franka and RBY1 robots shows that MolmoB0T models, despite never seeing real data, generalize robustly to novel environments and adversarial perturbations.

talks.session_title: Oral O3: Data, simulation and evaluation
talks.title: What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation?
talks.affiliation: Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago, University of Chicago, Argonne National Laboratory
talks.summary: This paper critically examines current robot manipulation benchmarks, identifying four ways that high scores can be misleading: shortcuts, noise, tuning to fixed tests, and data that mimics generalization. The authors propose more rigorous evaluation protocols, including testing after release and using wider, more diverse test sets.

subsections.title: Four Ways Benchmark Scores Mislead
subsections.visual_caption: Slide listing the four pitfalls: shortcuts, noise, fixed test tuning, and data-driven 'generalization'.
subsections.summary: The speaker argues that high benchmark scores often reflect memorization or exploitation of fixed test distributions rather than true robotic capability or generalization.

subsections.title: Case Studies: LIBERO and CALVIN
subsections.visual_caption: Bar chart showing a simple MLP policy matching state-of-the-art VLA performance on LIBERO.
subsections.summary: The authors demonstrate that simple policies without pre-training or language understanding can achieve near-SOTA results on popular benchmarks by exploiting narrow test distributions.

subsections.title: Proposed Solutions for Rigorous Evaluation
subsections.visual_caption: Graph showing the confidence intervals required to prove a policy is truly better than a baseline.
subsections.summary: The talk concludes with recommendations for the community, such as hiding test sets until after model release and providing clear guidance on the statistical significance of performance gaps.

subsections.title: Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Speaker answering questions about benchmark overfitting.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses how large language models can overfit to fixed benchmarks and suggests adaptive testing methods to find the true boundaries of policy capability.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Monday Early PM
talks.title: Scaling Robotic Dexterity Toward Real-World Applications
talks.summary: Sharpa presents their 'Three Paths, One Shared Stack' approach to scaling robotic dexterity. The talk covers hardware-software co-design for tactile sensing, decoupling motion intent from interaction through a multi-layered control system, and cross-embodiment learning using tactile tokens to transfer skills between different robotic platforms.

subsections.title: Introduction & Motivation
subsections.visual_caption: Three Paths to Scalable Dexterity overview slide.
subsections.summary: Reed Lu introduces Sharpa's mission and identifies the data pipeline as the primary bottleneck in scaling general-purpose robotic dexterity.

subsections.title: Path 1: Hardware & Software Co-design
subsections.visual_caption: Sharpa's hardware stack including the WO2 hand and D01 robot.
subsections.summary: Details on Sharpa's custom hardware stack, including the WO2 dexterous hand with 21 degrees of freedom and full-hand tactile sensing, and the AE01 teleoperation glove.

subsections.title: Path 2: Decoupling Motion Intent from Interaction
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the multi-layered control system (System 0, 1, and 2).
subsections.summary: Introduction of CraftNet and a hierarchical control architecture that separates high-level task reasoning from fast, tactile-driven interaction layers.

subsections.title: Path 3: Tactile Tokens for Cross-Embodiment Transfer
subsections.visual_caption: FTP-1 framework for cross-embodiment tactile representation.
subsections.summary: Explaining the FTP-1 framework, which maps diverse tactile modalities into a shared token space to enable skill transfer across different sensors and robot embodiments.

subsections.title: Growth Journey & Real-World Deployment
subsections.visual_caption: Sharpa's product evolution timeline and DQ ice cream store demo.
subsections.summary: A review of Sharpa's rapid development timeline and their deployment of a fully autonomous robotic ice cream store in collaboration with Dairy Queen.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Monday Early PM
talks.title: Scaling Robot Learning Through Data and Simulation
talks.summary: Lightwheel discusses their continuous learning infrastructure for physical AI, focusing on bridging the reality gap through high-fidelity simulation. They introduce EgoSuite for large-scale egocentric data and RoboFinals for standardized RL evaluation, emphasizing the importance of physics-grounded simulation for scaling robot learning.

subsections.title: Continuous Learning Infrastructure
subsections.visual_caption: Lightwheel's continuous learning loop diagram.
subsections.summary: Christian Ureno outlines the need for a closed-loop infrastructure that integrates real-world data, simulation, and deployment feedback.

subsections.title: Training & Evaluation Pyramids
subsections.visual_caption: The Training Pyramid and Evaluation Pyramid slides.
subsections.summary: A conceptual framework for scaling learning from human experience to simulation and finally to real-robot deployment.

subsections.title: SimFoundry: Real2Sim Pipeline
subsections.visual_caption: The Physics Measurement Factory for Real2Sim calibration.
subsections.summary: Details on SimFoundry, which uses a physics measurement factory to calibrate simulation parameters like friction and damping for high-fidelity Real2Sim transfer.

subsections.title: EgoSuite: Scalable Egocentric Data
subsections.visual_caption: EgoSuite-Open100K dataset overview.
subsections.summary: Introduction of the EgoSuite-Open100K dataset, a massive multimodal egocentric dataset designed for pre-training foundation models for robotics.

subsections.title: RoboFinals: RL Environments & Benchmarks
subsections.visual_caption: RoboFinals live evaluation benchmark on Newton.
subsections.summary: Showcasing RoboFinals, a suite of RL environments and benchmarks that allow for parallel, real-time evaluation of robotic policies at scale.

subsections.title: Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Christian Ureno answering questions from the audience.
subsections.summary: Discussion on simulating surface friction and damping using the SimFoundry measurement factory.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Monday Early PM
talks.title: From Dreaming to Doing: World Action Models and Agentic Robotics
talks.summary: Jim Fan concludes his keynote on GR00T-2, a foundation model for humanoid robots that unifies cognition and action. He details the WAM API for visual steering and the ASPIRE framework for error recovery, while announcing the open-sourcing of model weights and simulation tools to support the humanoid robotics community.

subsections.title: The 'Astra' Moment & System 1 Models
subsections.visual_caption: The '5 Stages of Grief' for roboticists after the release of Astra.
subsections.summary: Jim Fan discusses the impact of large language models on robotics and the emergence of fast, reactive System 1 models like Jev.

subsections.title: Groot 2: World-Action Model Architecture
subsections.visual_caption: Groot 2 World-Action Model architecture diagram.
subsections.summary: Explaining the architecture of Groot 2, a 2-billion parameter model that jointly decodes actions and predicted future video frames.

subsections.title: X-Adapt: Cross-Embodiment Skill Transfer
subsections.visual_caption: Zero-shot transfer from human UMI data to a real robot.
subsections.summary: Demonstrating X-Adapt, which allows skills learned from easy-to-collect human data (UMI, mocap) to be transferred zero-shot to real robots.

subsections.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Isaac Lab
subsections.visual_caption: RL training in Isaac Lab and transfer to real-world kitchen tasks.
subsections.summary: Showcasing how Groot 2 can be trained in simulation using Isaac Lab and transferred to real-world environments like kitchens and cafes.

subsections.title: Unified Cognition & WAM API
subsections.visual_caption: WAM API visual steering for solving the Tower of Hanoi.
subsections.summary: Introduction of the WAM API, which enables high-level reasoning models to steer low-level action models through visual guidance on pixels.

subsections.title: WAM Edit and Chemistry Lab Autonomy
subsections.visual_caption: Humanoid robot performing repetitive tasks in a chemistry lab setting.
subsections.summary: Jim Fan demonstrates WAM Edit, which allows for direct intervention in action execution, shown through autonomous tasks in a chemistry lab.

subsections.title: ASPIRE Agentic Harness and Error Recovery
subsections.visual_caption: Robot arms correcting an error while assembling a toy airplane wing.
subsections.summary: The ASPIRE agentic harness is presented, combining GR00T-2 with code-based skills to enable robust error recovery during complex assembly tasks.

subsections.title: Open Sourcing Model Weights and Simulation Engine
subsections.visual_caption: Slide announcing the open-sourcing of model weights and simulation tools.
subsections.summary: Jim Fan announces the open-sourcing of GR00T-2 model weights, the SimFoundry simulation engine, and the ASPIRE agentic harness.

subsections.title: Open Ecosystem and Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Group photo of the NVIDIA GR00T team.
subsections.summary: The talk concludes with an invitation to the community to build an open humanoid ecosystem, followed by a brief Q&A session.

talks.session_title: Early Career Keynote II — Negar Mehr
talks.title: How Can Robots Learn to Interact and Coordinate with Others?
talks.summary: The Q&A session for the first Early Career Keynote, focusing on the scalability of multi-agent data collection and the robustness of policies when transferring from simulation to real-world hardware.
talks.official_abstract: Robots in the real world rarely act alone. They share spaces with other robots and people, so they need to learn how to interact and coordinate. This talk explores multi-agent reinforcement learning with foundation model coaching, imitation of interacting agents, and formulating continual single-robot learning as consensus optimization.
talks.speaker_bio: Negar Mehr is an Assistant Professor of Mechanical Engineering at UC Berkeley, where she directs the Berkeley Intelligent Control (ICON) Lab. She received her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley and was a postdoc at Stanford University.

subsections.title: Introduction by Ken Goldberg
subsections.visual_caption: Ken Goldberg introducing Negar Mehr on stage.
subsections.summary: Session chair Ken Goldberg introduces Negar Mehr, highlighting her academic background and numerous awards in mechanical engineering and robotics.

subsections.title: Motivation: Robots in Unstructured Multi-Agent Environments
subsections.visual_caption: Video of Waymo autonomous vehicles navigating city streets in Austin.
subsections.summary: Negar Mehr motivates the need for robots to interact safely and intelligently with humans and other robots in unstructured, real-world environments.

subsections.title: Multi-Agent Imitation Learning and Diffusion Policies
subsections.visual_caption: MIMIC-D architecture diagram for multi-agent imitation learning.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the challenges of multi-agent imitation learning and introduces MIMIC-D, which uses decentralized diffusion policies to capture multi-modal coordination.

subsections.title: Coordination on Demand: The CRAFT Framework
subsections.visual_caption: CRAFT architecture diagram showing foundation models coaching reinforcement learning.
subsections.summary: Negar Mehr presents CRAFT, a framework that uses foundation models as coaches to enable multi-robot coordination by building on top of pretrained single-agent skills.

subsections.title: Real-Robot Experiments: Human-Robot Collaboration
subsections.visual_caption: A human and a quadruped robot collaboratively carrying a long wooden beam.
subsections.summary: The speaker demonstrates the effectiveness of her coordination methods through real-robot experiments involving quadrupeds and human-robot collaboration.

subsections.title: Continual Learning as Temporal Consensus (SAMBAR)
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram illustrating catastrophic forgetting in sequential task learning.
subsections.summary: Addressing catastrophic forgetting, Mehr introduces SAMBAR, which casts continual learning as reaching a temporal consensus between past and new policy parameters.

subsections.title: Dynamic Mapping with Temporal Consensus (TACO)
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of mapping results between TACO and baseline methods in a dynamic environment.
subsections.summary: The temporal consensus approach is applied to dynamic mapping (TACO), allowing robots to preserve static environment features while adapting to moved objects.

subsections.title: Scalability of Multi-agent Data Collection
subsections.visual_caption: Slido QR code for Q&A session.
subsections.summary: Discussion on the challenges of scaling up data for multi-agent interaction problems compared to single-agent domains.

subsections.title: Conclusion and Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: QR code on screen for the live Q&A session.
subsections.summary: Negar Mehr concludes her talk and begins a live Q&A session with the audience, discussing the scalability of multi-agent data collection.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: BitVLA: 1-bit Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotics Manipulation
talks.affiliation: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
talks.summary: BitVLA introduces the first fully native 1-bit Vision-Language-Action model, achieving significant reductions in memory usage and faster inference speeds while maintaining competitive performance on manipulation tasks.

subsections.title: Introduction to BitVLA and Performance Gains
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of BitVLA vs vanilla VLA showing 11x smaller memory and 4.4x faster speed.
subsections.summary: BitVLA uses ternary weights (-1, 0, +1) to reduce memory usage by 11x and increase inference speed by 4.4x compared to standard models.

subsections.title: BitLinear and Three-Stage Training
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the BitLinear layer architecture.
subsections.summary: The core component is BitLinear, which quantizes weights to 1.58 bits and activations to 8 bits, trained through a three-stage process including multimodal pre-training and distillation.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: EagleVLA: Towards Onboard Real-Time Robot Control via Foresight-Aligned Asynchronous Inference
talks.summary: EagleVLA addresses the challenges of deploying large VLA models on resource-constrained onboard devices by using foresight-aligned asynchronous inference to solve prediction-execution misalignment and long reaction times.

subsections.title: Challenges of Onboard VLA Deployment
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram illustrating prediction-execution misalignment due to latency.
subsections.summary: Long inference latency on onboard devices leads to misalignment between predicted actions and the current state of the world.

subsections.title: Foresight-Aligned Asynchronous Correction
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world demo of EagleVLA folding clothes compared to baselines.
subsections.summary: EagleVLA uses future environment prediction and confidence-based scheduling to achieve nearly 10x improvement in control frequency on edge hardware.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: REACT: Rolling Denoising and Dual Decoupling for Reactive Robot Control with VLA Models
talks.summary: REACT improves the reactivity of VLA policies by decoupling sensing, encoding, and execution, and using a rolling denoising process to incorporate fresh observations without losing temporal consistency.

subsections.title: The Reactivity vs. Consistency Trade-off
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of chunked VLA policies and dynamic reactivity.
subsections.summary: Standard action chunking provides consistency but limits reactivity when the environment changes during execution.

subsections.title: Rolling Denoising and Dual Decoupling
subsections.visual_caption: Robot demo showing REACT following a moving target (pouring rice).
subsections.summary: REACT uses rolling denoising to update action chunks with new observations and dual decoupling to maximize system throughput.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: TARC: Time-Adaptive Robotic Control
talks.summary: TARC proposes a method for robots to adaptively decide when to send control updates based on the situation, balancing efficiency and responsiveness rather than using a fixed control frequency.

subsections.title: Situational Control Frequency
subsections.visual_caption: Quadruped robot demo showing frequency spikes when the robot is pushed.
subsections.summary: TARC allows a robot to run at low frequency when stable and spike to high frequency only when reactive control is needed, such as when being pushed.

subsections.title: Budgeted Control Updates
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the TARC RL agent interaction loop.
subsections.summary: The problem is formulated as a constrained RL problem where the policy outputs both an action and a duration, optimizing performance under an explicit update budget.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: Diffusion ReRoll: Revisable Denoising for Robotic Sequential Prediction
talks.affiliation: Agency for Defense Development, Republic of Korea
talks.summary: Diffusion ReRoll introduces a structured denoising process that allows earlier parts of a predicted sequence to be revised based on later information, overcoming the limitations of causal denoising.

subsections.title: Revisable Denoising vs. Causal Denoising
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of noise levels across the prediction horizon for ReRoll.
subsections.summary: Unlike causal denoising which locks prefixes, Diffusion ReRoll keeps predictions open to revision, allowing cross-horizon information flow.

subsections.title: Performance on Long-horizon Tasks
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world navigation demo showing ReRoll handling OOD objects.
subsections.summary: The method shows significant improvements in long-horizon planning and policy learning, particularly in situations where early decisions must account for later constraints.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: MoRE: Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Physics Robotic World Models
talks.summary: MoRE uses a mixture-of-experts architecture to create a unified 3D world model capable of generalizing across different materials (rigid and deformable) and interaction types.

subsections.title: Unified 3D World Model
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the MoRE architecture with motion and static encoders.
subsections.summary: MoRE addresses the limitation of existing models that only handle single materials by using specialized experts for different dynamic groups.

subsections.title: Generalization Across Materials
subsections.visual_caption: Real-robot demo showing MoRE manipulating rigid boxes and soft cloths.
subsections.summary: The model demonstrates strong performance in both simulation and real-world tasks, including multi-step manipulation of heterogeneous objects.

subsections.title: MoRE Architecture and Dynamics
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram of MoRE.
subsections.summary: The speaker re-explains the mixture-of-experts approach for handling rigid and deformable dynamics in a single model.

subsections.title: Real-world Manipulation Results
subsections.visual_caption: Robot demo manipulating a soft cloth and a rigid box.
subsections.summary: Demonstration of the model's ability to predict and control interactions with diverse materials in real-world settings.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: Targeting World Models to Compromise Robot Learning Pipelines
talks.summary: This work explores security vulnerabilities in robot learning pipelines, demonstrating how malicious data providers can poison robot policies by attacking the underlying world models through image perturbations.

subsections.title: Visual Prompt Hijacking
subsections.visual_caption: Example of an adversarial perturbation changing a 'safe' prompt to a 'dangerous' one.
subsections.summary: Attackers can inject malicious instructions into image frames that hijack the world model's generation, leading to dangerous behavior in the learned policy.

subsections.title: Backdoor Attacks in Transition Dynamics
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of a backdoor attack causing policy failure when a trigger is present.
subsections.summary: By altering transition dynamics, attackers can create backdoors where a policy performs correctly normally but fails or behaves maliciously when a specific visual trigger is observed.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: Chunk-wise Model-based Policy Optimization
talks.summary: CMPO optimizes model-based RL by using chunk-wise modeling to avoid the sequential cost and compounding errors of recurrent rollouts, leading to faster training and more stable gradients.

subsections.title: Recurrent Rollout Bottlenecks
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing compounding errors in sequential model calls.
subsections.summary: Traditional MBRL rollouts are computationally expensive and suffer from gradient instability due to backpropagation through time.

subsections.title: Collaborative Chunk-wise Modeling
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram of the collaborative chunk-wise modeling approach.
subsections.summary: CMPO maps current states and action chunks directly to future latent chunks in a single forward pass, achieving 30x faster inference and 50% reduction in training time.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S2: Efficient execution, world models and learning
talks.title: FedGuide: Diffusion Prior Alignment and Value Baseline Guidance for Heterogeneous Federated Reinforcement Learning
talks.summary: FedGuide addresses the challenge of heterogeneity in federated reinforcement learning by using diffusion priors and value baseline guidance to stabilize local policy updates across diverse robot clients.

subsections.title: Heterogeneity in Federated RL
subsections.visual_caption: Illustration of policy averaging failure due to diverse local objectives.
subsections.summary: Directly averaging local policies in federated settings is fragile because diverse local objectives can erase specialized behavior modes.

subsections.title: Diffusion Prior Alignment
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing personalized diffusion priors aligned by optimal transport.
subsections.summary: FedGuide uses optimal transport to align personalized diffusion priors and a state-only value baseline to reduce variance and improve final returns.

talks.session_title: Keynote I — Wolfram Burgard
talks.title: Challenges to Realize Embodied AI
talks.summary: Wolfram Burgard discusses the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models into robotics for complex task decomposition, semantic grasping, and force control. He emphasizes the importance of tactile sensing and multimodal data for robust interaction with the real world.
talks.official_abstract: To achieve Embodied Artificial Intelligence, we need robots that can robustly perceive their environments and execute actions under sensor and actuator uncertainty. This presentation discusses combining probabilistic and deep-learning approaches to robotics and utilizing foundation models in complex, changing real-world environments.
talks.speaker_bio: Wolfram Burgard is Professor of Computer Science at the University of Technology Nuremberg. Previously Professor at the University of Freiburg and VP for Automated Driving and ML at Toyota Research Institute, he is a recipient of the IEEE RAS Pioneer Award and Leibniz Prize.

subsections.title: Introduction by Dieter Fox
subsections.visual_caption: Dieter Fox introducing the keynote speaker.
subsections.summary: Session chair Dieter Fox introduces Wolfram Burgard, highlighting his extensive contributions to robotics, including his work on probabilistic robotics and his leadership roles in the IEEE Robotics and Automation Society.

subsections.title: Societal Challenges & Intelligent Embodied Robots
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram for AI as the key factor for embodiment.
subsections.summary: Wolfram Burgard outlines the societal challenges robotics can address, such as traffic, production, and healthcare, and defines the core loop of intelligent embodied robots: perceive, model, and act.

subsections.title: The Sisyphus Metaphor & Three Boulders of Robotics
subsections.visual_caption: Painting of Sisyphus pushing a boulder up a hill.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces the Sisyphus metaphor to represent the robotics community's journey, identifying three major technological 'boulders': Probabilistic Robotics, Deep Networks, and Foundation Models.

subsections.title: Boulder 1: Probabilistic Robotics & Autonomous Driving
subsections.visual_caption: Cover of the 'Probabilistic Robotics' book by Thrun, Burgard, and Fox.
subsections.summary: This section covers the era of probabilistic robotics, focusing on state estimation and uncertainty, which led to significant successes in autonomous driving and high-accuracy 3D mapping (SLAM).

subsections.title: Boulder 2: Deep Networks & Uncertainty-Aware Perception
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of uncertainty-aware panoptic segmentation.
subsections.summary: The talk transitions to the deep learning era, emphasizing the improvement in semantic interpretation of sensor data while noting the ongoing challenge of integrating these networks with probabilistic state estimation through calibrated uncertainties.

subsections.title: Boulder 3: Foundation Models & Language-Grounded Navigation
subsections.visual_caption: Title slide for Visual Language Maps for Robot Navigation (VLMaps).
subsections.summary: Burgard discusses the impact of foundation models, demonstrating how they enable zero-shot, language-guided navigation and open-vocabulary mapping, potentially reducing the reliance on rigid geometric HD maps.

subsections.title: Semantic Pathways & Affordance Learning
subsections.visual_caption: Title slide for LAN-Grasp: Semantic Object Grasping.
subsections.summary: The presentation explores using Large Language Models (LLMs) as programming assistants to decompose complex instructions into elementary robot skills and learning object affordances from unstructured play data.

subsections.title: LAN-Grasp: Semantic Object Grasping
subsections.visual_caption: LAN-Grasp system architecture diagram using LLMs for semantic object grasping.
subsections.summary: Introduction of LAN-Grasp, a system that leverages LLMs to identify semantic parts of objects, such as the handle of a mug, to enable more natural and functional grasping.

subsections.title: Zero-Shot Semantic Grasping Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Grid of robot hardware demos performing semantic grasps on various objects like dolls and candles.
subsections.summary: Demonstration of the system's ability to perform semantic grasps on novel objects in a zero-shot fashion, showing robustness across different object categories.

subsections.title: FlowTouch: Predicting Tactile Sensor Signals
subsections.visual_caption: FlowTouch model architecture for view-invariant visuo-tactile prediction.
subsections.summary: Introduction of FlowTouch, a method to predict tactile sensor signals from visual data, which helps in planning stable grasps and understanding object properties before contact.

subsections.title: Wrench-ACT: Force Control in Manipulation
subsections.visual_caption: Wrench-ACT policy architecture for contact-rich behavior using direct wrench control.
subsections.summary: The speaker argues for explicit force/torque control in robot policies to handle contact-rich tasks more reliably than traditional position control.

subsections.title: Interpreting and Steering Vision-Language Navigation
subsections.visual_caption: Heatmaps showing visual and textual focus of Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) models.
subsections.summary: Analysis of what Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) models actually rely on and the introduction of activation steering to correct out-of-domain behavior.

subsections.title: Infrastructure and Benchmarks for Robot Learning
subsections.visual_caption: Slide detailing the Open X-Embodiment project and robotic foundation models.
subsections.summary: Discussion on the necessity of large-scale compute infrastructure and standardized benchmarks like DuoBench for advancing bimanual manipulation research.

subsections.title: Keynote Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Wolfram Burgard answering questions from the audience.
subsections.summary: Wolfram Burgard answers questions regarding the challenges of data collection for force control and the future of imitation learning in complex environments.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Monday Late PM
talks.title: General Motors Diamond Sponsor Talk
talks.summary: Sean Harris from GM discusses the integration of Reinforcement Learning (RL) self-play and Imitation Learning for autonomous driving. He highlights how GM uses these technologies in production to achieve human-like driving behavior while maintaining robustness through simulation-based self-play and large-scale human driving datasets.

subsections.title: Introduction to GM Autonomy
subsections.visual_caption: Title slide for Innovations in Autonomy at GM.
subsections.summary: Introduction of Sean Harris and the formation of the GM Autonomy team, combining expertise from Cruise and Super Cruise.

subsections.title: Vision for Personal Autonomy
subsections.visual_caption: GM autonomous vehicle driving on a highway.
subsections.summary: Discussing the goal of providing safety and time back to drivers through 'eyes-off' highway products scheduled for launch in 2028.

subsections.title: RL Self-Play in Simulation
subsections.visual_caption: Slide explaining RL Self-Play for learning to drive in simulation.
subsections.summary: Explaining how GM uses reinforcement learning with self-play in high-speed simulation environments to learn robust driving behaviors at scale.

subsections.title: RL Self-Play and Imitation Learning
subsections.visual_caption: Slide comparing RL Self-Play strengths and weaknesses.
subsections.summary: Explains the use of RL self-play for scaling and coverage in simulation, and imitation learning to match real-world distributions and human-like behavior.

subsections.title: Combining Imitation and Self-Play
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing three ways to combine Imitation and Self-Play.
subsections.summary: Discusses strategies for merging these techniques, such as using human policy as an anchor, distillation, or learning rewards from human driving.

subsections.title: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in Driving
subsections.visual_caption: VLM-based driving decisions for crash scenes and traffic stops.
subsections.summary: Demonstrates how VLMs are used for high-level scene understanding and reasoning, such as identifying police vehicles and deciding to change lanes.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Monday Late PM
talks.title: BitRobot: RoboCap & RoboColosseum
talks.summary: BitRobot introduces RoboCap, a wearable data collection device, and RoboColosseum, a large-scale open evaluation effort for physical AI. They showcase several open-source datasets including RoboCap-10K and HIW-500, aiming to crowdsource real-world entropy to advance robot learning.

subsections.title: RoboCap Hardware Ecosystem
subsections.visual_caption: Exploded view of the RoboCap wearable camera system.
subsections.summary: Michael Cho introduces RoboCap, a head-mounted device with 6 cameras and 2 IMUs, and the RoboWrist combo for manipulation-level data capture.

subsections.title: Open-Source Datasets: RoboCap-10K and HIW-500
subsections.visual_caption: Global map showing data collection points for the FrodoBots dataset.
subsections.summary: Presents massive datasets including 10,000 hours of occupational work, 500 hours of humanoid-in-the-wild data, and urban navigation data from 56 countries.

subsections.title: RoboColosseum: Measuring Physical Intelligence
subsections.visual_caption: RoboColosseum leaderboard comparing various VLA models.
subsections.summary: Jiafei Duan introduces RoboColosseum, a shared foundation for standardized, large-scale physical evaluation of robot models in diverse real-world environments.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Monday Late PM
talks.title: MaxInsights: Building Data Infrastructure for Physical AI
talks.summary: MaxInsights presents their data infrastructure for training and evaluating physical AI, focusing on high-quality egocentric data. They introduce MaxCAPE, a fine-grained egocentric dataset with finger-level contact and action phase annotations, and demonstrate their data feedback loop for robot learning in the wild.

subsections.title: Scaling Real-World Experience
subsections.visual_caption: MaxInsights data scale and quality metrics slide.
subsections.summary: Kun Wang discusses the transition from teleoperation to scalable egocentric foundation models, having collected over 1 million hours of data.

subsections.title: MaxCAPE: Fine-grained Egocentric Data
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison table of MaxCAPE vs other egocentric datasets.
subsections.summary: Introduces MaxCAPE, which provides sub-second action segmentation and finger-level contact labels to improve dexterous manipulation learning.

subsections.title: Language Annotation and Benchmarking
subsections.visual_caption: Max Reasoning Model monitoring robot actions on an elevator panel.
subsections.summary: Explains the importance of goal clarity and temporal consistency in language annotations, and demonstrates a reasoning model providing corrective feedback to robots.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: Ego2Robot: Scalable Robot Data Synthesis from Egocentric Human Data
talks.affiliation: AIM3 Lab, Renmin University of China; Qwen Team, Alibaba Inc.
talks.summary: This paper introduces Ego2Robot, a pipeline that synthesizes robot training data from egocentric human videos by aligning actions and visual appearance. The method bridges the human-to-robot gap by retargeting hand motion to robot grippers and inpainting robot arms into human scenes, significantly improving foundation model pre-training for diverse tasks.

subsections.title: Motivation & Action/Vision Alignment
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing the bridging of the human-to-robot gap through retargeting and inpainting.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains the difficulty of using diverse human video data for robot learning and introduces the Ego2Robot approach for action and vision alignment.

subsections.title: Pipeline at Scale & Evaluation
subsections.visual_caption: Grid of synthesized robot data clips across 15 robot morphologies.
subsections.summary: The talk details the scaling of the synthesis pipeline to over 18,000 hours of data and presents results showing improvements in generalization across appearance, scene layout, and embodiment.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: Learning Human Intention for Robotic Manipulation
talks.summary: This work proposes a framework to learn human intention from gaze data to improve robotic manipulation. By predicting intention tokens before generating action sequences, the model creates a 'chain of thought' that enables more efficient transfer of high-level skills from human data to robots.

subsections.title: Motivation & Intention-Action Loop
subsections.visual_caption: Illustration of the perception-intention-action loop in humans.
subsections.summary: The presenter discusses the embodiment gap and argues that high-level intentions learned from human gaze transfer more easily to robots than direct actions.

subsections.title: VLIA Model & Experiments
subsections.visual_caption: The VLIA model pipeline showing pre-training, post-training, and deployment stages.
subsections.summary: The talk describes the three-stage pipeline (VLIA) and presents real-world experiments where modeling intention improves task success rates and adaptation.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: Efficient and Reliable Teleoperation through Real-to-Sim-to-Real Shared Autonomy
talks.summary: This paper presents a shared autonomy approach using a residual copilot to make teleoperation more reliable for fine-grained, contact-rich tasks. The copilot is trained in simulation using a human surrogate fitted from minimal real-world data, allowing human operators to focus on high-level intent while the system manages low-level forces.

subsections.title: Problem: Fine-grained Teleoperation
subsections.visual_caption: Demos of challenging tasks like nut threading and gear meshing.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights how traditional teleoperation breaks down for high-precision tasks due to latency and lack of force feedback.

subsections.title: Shared Autonomy & Residual Copilot
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram explaining the combination of high-level human intent and low-level RL control.
subsections.summary: The talk introduces the residual copilot concept and the real-to-sim-to-real pipeline used to train it without a human in the loop.

subsections.title: Results & User Study
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of success rates and completion times across different teleoperation methods.
subsections.summary: The presenter shows that the copilot improves success rates and user satisfaction across various tasks while following the operator's intent.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: FlowDAgger: Human-in-the-Loop Adaptation of Generative Robot Policies in Latent Space
talks.affiliation: Microsoft Research, University of Washington, ETH Zurich
talks.summary: FlowDAgger is a method for rapidly adapting pre-trained generative robot policies using human-in-the-loop corrections in latent space. By using action inversion to map human corrections back to the latent space, the system can steer foundation models toward success in just a few episodes without expensive full-model fine-tuning.

subsections.title: Latent Space Learning with Human-in-the-Loop
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of FlowDAgger adapting flow matching and diffusion models.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains the goal of learning from human corrections to steer noise-conditioned policies toward successful action distributions.

subsections.title: Action Inversion & Real-World Adaptation
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world robot demo of toolbox packing being adapted with FlowDAgger.
subsections.summary: The talk details the action inversion technique and presents results showing significant performance gains on downstream tasks with minimal human intervention.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: BiDexGrasp: Coordinated Bimanual Dexterous Grasps across Object Geometries and Sizes
talks.summary: BiDexGrasp addresses the challenge of coordinated bimanual dexterous grasping for large or irregular objects. The framework includes an efficient data synthesis pipeline that is 40x faster than baselines and a bimanual coordination module that enables stable grasping across diverse object geometries and sizes.

subsections.title: Motivation: Bimanual Dexterous Grasping
subsections.visual_caption: Robotic hands attempting to grasp large and irregular objects.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains why large objects require two hands and the limitations of existing datasets for bimanual grasping.

subsections.title: Data Synthesis & Coordination Module
subsections.visual_caption: The BiDexGrasp pipeline showing data synthesis and grasp generation components.
subsections.summary: The talk describes the synthesis pipeline, the bimanual coordination module, and real-world validation results achieving high success rates.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: KPGrasp: Scalable Keypoint Flow Matching for Dexterous Grasp Generation
talks.affiliation: Peking University, Gaibot, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Tsinghua University
talks.summary: KPGrasp introduces a scalable keypoint flow matching method for dexterous grasp generation. By representing grasps with 3D keypoints and using a Diffusion Transformer (DIT), the model learns grasp distributions directly from data, significantly outperforming analytical and previous learning-based methods in success rate and penetration depth.

subsections.title: Keypoint Representation for Grasping
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of traditional parameterization vs. 3D keypoint representation.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the paradigms of grasp generation and introduces 3D keypoints as a way to avoid kinematic error accumulation.

subsections.title: DIT Architecture & Benchmark Results
subsections.visual_caption: Benchmark results on Dexonomy and DexGrasp Anything datasets.
subsections.summary: The talk details the three-stage method using a conditional DIT and presents results showing high-quality grasps across challenging geometries.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: WM-Craftnet: World Synesthesia Model for Robust and Generalizable Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
talks.summary: WM-Craftnet presents a World Synesthesia Model (WSM) for robust and generalizable in-hand manipulation. The model integrates depth, touch, and proprioception to reconstruct clean state representations from noisy sensor inputs, enabling a single policy to rotate diverse objects and recover from external disturbances.

subsections.title: World Synesthesia Model (WSM)
subsections.visual_caption: Methodology diagram showing the integration of depth, touch, and proprioception.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces the WSM, a recurrent state space model that reconstructs clean depth and tactile data from noisy inputs.

subsections.title: Robust Rotation & Generalization Results
subsections.visual_caption: Key takeaways slide summarizing world model capabilities.
subsections.summary: The talk presents experiments on diverse axis rotation and zero-shot transfer to unseen objects, demonstrating the model's robustness.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: Sequential Asymmetric Imitation for Learning Coupled Robot Policies
talks.summary: This paper proposes Sequential Asymmetric Imitation (SAI) for learning coupled robot policies in collaborative manipulation tasks.
