By training robots to respond to their partner's progress and mistakes through visual observations, the method enables effective coordination without explicit inter-robot communication.

subsections.title: Challenge: Physically Coupled Coordination
subsections.visual_caption: Examples of coordination failures in collaborative tasks like bed-throw spreading.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses how independent policies can get out of sync and the requirement for robots to respond to their partner's progress.

subsections.title: Sequential Asymmetric Imitation (SAI)
subsections.visual_caption: The SAI pipeline showing skill bootstrapping and partner adaptation stages.
subsections.summary: The talk details the SAI teaching process and presents results showing improved success rates across various collaborative tasks.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S3: Human learning, dexterity and cooperation
talks.title: Leave It Better Than Found: Value-Guided Cooperation in Sequential Tasks
talks.summary: This work introduces PAVE, a method for value-guided cooperation in sequential tasks where robots modify a shared environment. By sharing value functions, a leader robot can optimize handoff states to 'leave the world better' for a follower robot, improving overall system success in ad-hoc scenarios.

subsections.title: Sequential Task Continuation Problem
subsections.visual_caption: Example of a leader robot blocking a follower's path by moving a box.
subsections.summary: The speaker defines the problem where a follower robot inherits a state modified by a leader, potentially leading to failure if not coordinated.

subsections.title: PAVE: Policy Adaptation via Value Exchange
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram explaining the PAVE method and value exchange mechanism.
subsections.summary: The talk describes the PAVE method, which uses shared value functions to guide the leader's actions online, and demonstrates its effectiveness on real robots.

talks.session_title: Oral O4: Reinforcement learning and motion reasoning
talks.title: RL Token: Bootstrapping Online RL with Vision-Language-Action Models
talks.summary: This paper introduces RL Token, a method to bootstrap online reinforcement learning using Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. It uses an encoder-decoder to compress VLA image embeddings into a single token for downstream RL and conditions the RL actor on VLA action proposals to improve sample efficiency. Results show significant speedups in precision tasks like zip-tie threading and Ethernet insertion compared to supervised fine-tuning.

subsections.title: Motivation: Improving VLA for Real-World Deployment
subsections.visual_caption: Demos of VLA models performing diverse tasks like coffee making and box assembly.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the impressive capabilities of current VLA models but notes their limitations in precision and reliability for real-world deployment.

subsections.title: Motivation: VLA Failures in Precision Tasks
subsections.visual_caption: Video showing a robot failing to thread a zip-tie due to minor misalignment.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses how current VLA models fail in precise and deformable object manipulation where tiny errors are amplified, necessitating online RL for improvement.

subsections.title: RL Token Method & Comparison to RECAP
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison slide between RECAP and the proposed RL Token method.
subsections.summary: The talk introduces RL Token as a more computationally efficient alternative to full-model fine-tuning for targeted task improvement.

subsections.title: Method: RL Token Information Bottleneck
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram of the encoder-decoder network for feature compression.
subsections.summary: The method trains an encoder-decoder to compress high-dimensional VLA image embeddings into a single RL token that serves as an observation input for downstream RL.

subsections.title: Method: Action Bootstrap & Actor Loss
subsections.visual_caption: Mathematical formulation of the actor objective with behavior regularization.
subsections.summary: To avoid distribution collapse, the RL actor is conditioned on VLA action proposals and uses a behavior cloning term in the actor loss.

subsections.title: Experiments: Precision Assembly & Zip-tie Threading
subsections.visual_caption: Robot hardware demo of aligning a screwdriver onto a screw using RLT.
subsections.summary: Real-world experiments demonstrate that RLT enables robots to solve challenging bottlenecks in assembly tasks much faster than supervised fine-tuning.

subsections.title: Results: Ethernet Insertion Speedup
subsections.visual_caption: Histogram comparing episode lengths of teleoperation, base model, and RLT.
subsections.summary: RLT achieves a median episode length of 66 steps for Ethernet insertion, outperforming even experienced human teleoperators.

subsections.title: Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Charles Xu answering questions from the audience.
subsections.summary: The speaker clarifies the information bottleneck design and confirms that the RL token provides a 2x speed improvement over standard vision encoders.

talks.session_title: Oral O4: Reinforcement learning and motion reasoning
talks.title: Flow Policy Gradients for Robot Control
talks.summary: This work presents FPO++, an improved version of Flow Policy Gradients for robot control. It addresses stability issues in the original FPO by introducing per-sample trust regions and an asymmetric trust region (ASPO) to regularize the posterior gap for negative advantages. The method demonstrates stable training across quadruped locomotion, humanoid motion tracking, and complex manipulation tasks.

subsections.title: Prior Work: FPO and Stability Issues
subsections.visual_caption: Slide summarizing prior work on reinforcement learning with flow matching.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces the original FPO algorithm and shows how it fails to train stably in complex robotics tasks despite hyperparameter tuning.

subsections.title: Method: FPO++ Per-sample Trust Regions & ASPO
subsections.visual_caption: Equations for per-sample clipping and the ASPO objective.
subsections.summary: FPO++ introduces per-sample clipping for finer-grained trust regions and ASPO to handle negative advantages without increasing the posterior gap.

subsections.title: Experiments: Quadruped & Humanoid Locomotion
subsections.visual_caption: Video of a G1 humanoid robot performing dynamic whole-body motion tracking.
subsections.summary: The method is validated on diverse locomotion tasks, showing stable training and the emergence of semantic joint correlations like torso-hip coordination.

subsections.title: Results: Manipulation Fine-tuning & Zero-sampling
subsections.visual_caption: Benchmark curves for fine-tuning pretrained manipulation policies.
subsections.summary: FPO++ achieves state-of-the-art returns on image-based manipulation tasks and highlights the importance of zero-sampling for reliable deployment.

subsections.title: Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Hongsuk Choi answering questions about multimodality.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains how flow matching preserves exploration during training while zero-sampling ensures smooth trajectories during inference.

talks.session_title: Oral O4: Reinforcement learning and motion reasoning
talks.title: Driving, Fast or Slow? Neuro-Symbolic Guidance for Motion Prediction in Multi-Modal Ground Mobility
talks.summary: This paper proposes TraCS (Trajectory Compliance Shaping), a neuro-symbolic framework for motion prediction in multi-modal ground mobility. It uses an agentic coding loop to translate natural language traffic rules into probabilistic logic programs that reshape neural trajectory proposals. Evaluation on the Argoverse 2 dataset shows improved prediction accuracy, particularly for long-tail cases like pedestrians and buses.

subsections.title: Motivation: Heterogeneous Traffic & Black-box Models
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing different traffic participant classes and their specific rules.
subsections.summary: The speakers highlight the difficulty of predicting diverse traffic participants using black-box neural models that lack explicit rule encoding.

subsections.title: Method: TraCS - Trajectory Compliance Shaping
subsections.visual_caption: System architecture diagram showing the fusion of neural proposals and symbolic rules.
subsections.summary: TraCS reshapes neural trajectory proposals by fusing them with a probabilistic symbolic model of local traffic laws in a log-linear opinion pool.

subsections.title: Method: Agentic Coding Loop (Natural Language to Logic)
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the iterative coding loop involving a coder, judge, and verifier.
subsections.summary: An agentic loop uses LLMs to translate legal text into logic programs, with a judge and verifier ensuring semantic and syntactic correctness.

subsections.title: Experiments: Compliance Landscapes & Argoverse 2
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of a compliance landscape map for moving agents.
subsections.summary: The framework generates compliance landscapes that evaluate the probability of following rules at every location, tested on 25,000 Argoverse 2 samples.

subsections.title: Results: Long-tail Improvements for Pedestrians
subsections.visual_caption: Bar charts showing error reduction across different road user classes.
subsections.summary: TraCS significantly improves predictions for vulnerable road users like pedestrians by leveraging their tendency to follow specific rules in safety-critical scenarios.

subsections.title: Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Simon Kohaut and Felix Divo answering questions about rule conflicts.
subsections.summary: The presenters discuss handling conflicting rules and the scalability of checking multiple road participants simultaneously using statistical spatial relations.

talks.session_title: Early Career Keynote III — Roberto Martín-Martín
talks.title: Learning Without Starting Over: Expanding What Robots Can Learn in the Real World
talks.summary: Roberto Martin-Martin presents a framework for expanding a robot's 'learning potential'—the ability to acquire new capabilities with minimal real-world data. He details research into structured action spaces (SLAC), safe imitation from single human videos (SafeMimic), damage-aware simulation (OopsieVerse), and algorithmic data selection (DataMIL/GUILD) to enable continuous improvement without starting from scratch.
talks.official_abstract: As foundation models expand what robots can already do, an equally important question is how to expand their learning potential: learning reusable action spaces for safe physical exploration, using human demonstrations and corrections for real-world refinement, and selecting experience according to policy improvement.
talks.speaker_bio: Roberto Martín-Martín is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at UT Austin, where he directs the Robot Interactive Intelligence Lab (RobIn). He earned his Ph.D. at TU Berlin and was a postdoc at Stanford SVL.

subsections.title: Introduction & Keith Jarrett Story
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing Keith Jarrett and the Köln Concert album cover.
subsections.summary: The speaker tells the story of Keith Jarrett adapting to a faulty piano to create a masterpiece, illustrating how experts must learn to handle new constraints.

subsections.title: Intro & Motivation: Defining Learning Potential
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of developmental psychology in infants vs robot hammering experiments.
subsections.summary: Roberto introduces the concept of 'learning potential' as the difference between current capabilities and what can be learned with finite data, arguing that robots should be equipped with structures that make future learning easier.

subsections.title: Developmental Psychology: Learning to Hammer
subsections.visual_caption: Video of a baby learning to use a toy hammer.
subsections.summary: The talk transitions to developmental psychology, asking when the learning process for a specific skill actually begins in humans.

subsections.title: Learning-Enabling Action Spaces (SLAC)
subsections.visual_caption: Grid of four contact-rich mobile manipulation tasks solved by SLAC in under one hour.
subsections.summary: The speaker presents SLAC, which learns a task-agnostic latent action space in simulation to enable much faster and safer reinforcement learning on real robots for complex manipulation tasks.

subsections.title: Safe Imitation from Human Guidance (SafeMimic)
subsections.visual_caption: Evaluation of SafeMimic across seven physical tasks including navigation and manipulation.
subsections.summary: Roberto discusses SafeMimic, a method for robots to learn multi-step tasks from a single human video by parsing semantics and motion, then safely adapting the behavior to their own embodiment using simulation-learned safety priors.

subsections.title: Task-Agnostic Safety Signals (OopsieVerse)
subsections.visual_caption: OopsieVerse framework showing unified safety signals for impact, water, and fire damage.
subsections.summary: To provide the safety signals needed for pre-training, the speaker introduces OopsieVerse, a framework that models real-world damage in simulation by tracking the 'health' of objects.

subsections.title: Learning Transferable Corrections (OopsieRecover)
subsections.visual_caption: Pipeline for parsing human corrections into semantically grounded programmatic costs.
subsections.summary: OopsieRecover is presented as a way to extract reusable lessons from human interventions, allowing a robot to generalize a handful of corrections to new, unseen failure situations.

subsections.title: Algorithmic Data Selection & Collection (DataMIL/GUILD)
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture of DataMIL for selecting the best subset of data to train a performant policy.
subsections.summary: The talk concludes with methods for identifying useful experience from large datasets (DataMIL) and guiding autonomous data collection (GUILD) to maximize the performance of a target task policy.

subsections.title: Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Roberto Martin-Martin answering questions from the conference audience.
subsections.summary: Roberto answers audience questions regarding the transfer of safety knowledge from simulation to the real world and the current limitations of formal safety guarantees in complex environments.

talks.session_title: Oral O5: Dexterous learning, grasping and assembly
talks.title: EgoScale: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation with Diverse Egocentric Human Data
talks.summary: EgoScale addresses the high cost of robot teleoperation data by leveraging abundant human egocentric video for pre-training. It uses a three-stage training recipe—human pre-training, aligned mid-training with paired human-robot data, and task-specific post-training—to enable high-success dexterous manipulation and one-shot transfer to new tasks.

subsections.title: Motivation and Large-Scale Egocentric Dataset
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the 20,854-hour egocentric video dataset.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces the challenge of expensive robot data and presents a massive 20,000+ hour dataset of human egocentric videos covering diverse tasks and interactions.

subsections.title: Addressing Visual and Embodiment Gaps
subsections.visual_caption: Aligned human and robot data collection setup.
subsections.summary: To bridge the gap between human and robot data, the authors introduce an aligned mid-training stage using paired data where humans wear sensors and cameras matching the robot's configuration.

subsections.title: Three-Stage Training and Experimental Results
subsections.visual_caption: Success rate comparison across five dexterous tasks.
subsections.summary: The talk details the three-stage training recipe and demonstrates that combining human pre-training with aligned mid-training significantly improves success rates on complex tasks like syringe manipulation.

subsections.title: Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Presenter answering questions from the audience.
subsections.summary: The presenter discusses the construction of paired robot data and confirms that human subjects were asked to mimic robot-like motions to ensure alignment.

talks.session_title: Oral O5: Dexterous learning, grasping and assembly
talks.title: OPENDEXGRASP: Open-vocabulary Task-Oriented Dexterous Grasping
talks.summary: OpenDexGrasp is a framework for generating task-oriented dexterous grasps from natural language instructions. It combines large-scale synthetic data for broad coverage with high-quality human demonstrations for functional alignment, using a vision-language model to predict task affordances and hand poses.

subsections.title: Functional Grasping and Data Ecosystem
subsections.visual_caption: Dual-source complementary data recipe: OpenDex-Scale and OpenDex-Align.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains that standard grasping methods often ignore task context and introduces a dual-source data approach combining 1.24M synthetic grasps with 27K human-demonstrated functional grasps.

subsections.title: Model Architecture and Task Affordance
subsections.visual_caption: Direct pose generation with shared functional grounding.
subsections.summary: The model uses a pre-trained VLM and a geometry encoder to connect language instructions to 3D object shapes, predicting both contact affordance and hand configuration.

subsections.title: Experimental Evaluation and Real-Robot Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world robot experiments with various everyday objects.
subsections.summary: The method achieves a 72% real-world grasp success rate across various objects and tasks, outperforming baselines in both simulation and human ratings for task suitability.

subsections.title: Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Presenter answering questions about contact forces.
subsections.summary: The presenter addresses failure modes related to object placement and explains how contact regions and forces are optimized together in the framework.

talks.session_title: Oral O5: Dexterous learning, grasping and assembly
talks.title: Play2Perfect: What Matters in Dexterous Play Pretraining for Precise Assembly?
talks.summary: Play2Perfect introduces a two-step learning framework for precise robotic assembly: task-agnostic play pre-training to acquire general dexterity, followed by rapid reinforcement learning fine-tuning for specific assembly tasks. This approach enables complex, long-horizon assembly with sub-millimeter precision and high robustness to perturbations.

subsections.title: The Challenge of Precise Assembly
subsections.visual_caption: Slow-motion breakdown of a table leg assembly task.
subsections.summary: The presenters demonstrate the difficulty of long-horizon assembly tasks like tight insertions and screwing, which pose significant exploration challenges for standard RL.

subsections.title: Play to Perfect Framework
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of task-agnostic play vs. assembly fine-tuning.
subsections.summary: Inspired by how children learn, the method first trains a robot to 'play' by reaching random 6D goal poses with diverse objects before fine-tuning on specific assembly tasks.

subsections.title: Training Efficiency and Robustness
subsections.visual_caption: Training efficiency curves showing 33x speedup over dense-reward RL.
subsections.summary: The authors show that play pre-training makes assembly fine-tuning 33x more efficient than training from scratch and results in more robust strategies that utilize multiple fingers.

subsections.title: Key Design Choices in Play Pre-training
subsections.visual_caption: Ablation study on goal precision and object diversity.
subsections.summary: The talk identifies four critical factors for successful play pre-training: 6D pose objectives, tight goal precision, high object diversity, and random trajectory sampling.

subsections.title: Real-World Deployment and Recovery
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world robot recovering from a dropped part during assembly.
subsections.summary: The system is deployed on real hardware using vision-based object tracking, demonstrating the ability to recover from initial failures and handle daily insertion tasks like plugging in a phone.

talks.session_title: Oral O6: Force, tactile control and manipulation planning
talks.title: FACTR 2: Learning External Force Sensing for Commodity Robot Arms Improves Policy Learning
talks.summary: FACTR 2 is a method designed to provide high-quality external force sensing for low-cost commodity robot arms without dedicated sensors. It utilizes two components: Neural External Torque Estimation (NEXT) for real-time torque prediction and Force-Informed Re-Sampling Training (FIRST) to improve behavior cloning policy performance on contact-rich tasks.

subsections.title: Neural External Torque Estimation (NEXT)
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the NEXT deployment process for external joint torque estimation.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains NEXT, which uses an LSTM trained on free-space motion data to predict robot dynamics. By calculating the residual error between predicted and measured torque during contact, the system estimates external forces without dedicated sensors.

subsections.title: Force-Informed Re-Sampling Training (FIRST)
subsections.visual_caption: Bar chart showing task progress improvements across various contact-rich tasks using FIRST.
subsections.summary: FIRST leverages estimated external torque to segment trajectories into free motion, pre-contact, and contact phases. Upsampling the critical pre-contact and contact segments during training significantly improves policy precision and recovery behaviors.

subsections.title: Summary and Conclusion
subsections.visual_caption: Summary slide illustrating the FACTR 2 framework and its impact on policy learning.
subsections.summary: The talk concludes by summarizing how FACTR 2 enables force-feedback teleoperation and robust policy learning for long-horizon tasks on low-cost hardware.

subsections.title: Live Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: The speaker answering audience questions about torque estimation and data collection.
subsections.summary: The speaker addresses questions regarding the impact of acceleration on torque estimation and the determination of optimal data collection times for training the NEXT model.

talks.session_title: Oral O6: Force, tactile control and manipulation planning
talks.title: PACE: Temporal-Role Tactile Conditioning for Chunk-Based Insertion Policies
talks.summary: PACE introduces a framework for temporal-role tactile conditioning in chunk-based insertion policies. By organizing tactile data into Phase, Event, and Prediction roles, the method improves the robot's ability to handle visually similar but contact-distinct states during precision insertion tasks.

subsections.title: Motivation: Contact Feedback in Insertion
subsections.visual_caption: Slide comparing visual alignment with contact-based feedback during insertion.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights the limitations of vision-only systems during the contact phase of insertion, where small misalignments can lead to failure, and argues for the necessity of effective tactile feedback.

subsections.title: PACE Framework: Phase, Event, and Prediction
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the PACE framework showing the three tactile pathways.
subsections.summary: The PACE framework organizes tactile information into three pathways: Phase for state-guided action generation, Event for rapid change detection and correction, and Prediction for auxiliary training signals.

subsections.title: Force-Feedback Demonstration Collection
subsections.visual_caption: Demonstration of the force-feedback teleoperation system used for data collection.
subsections.summary: A force-feedback teleoperation system using a Sigma.7 device is presented, which allows human operators to feel contact forces and provide more consistent demonstrations for training.

subsections.title: Evaluation and Results
subsections.visual_caption: Bar chart showing PACE's 90.7% success rate compared to vision-only and other tactile baselines.
subsections.summary: PACE is evaluated across five real-world insertion tasks, achieving a 90.7% success rate and significantly outperforming vision-only and standard tactile fusion baselines.

talks.session_title: Oral O6: Force, tactile control and manipulation planning
talks.title: Long-Horizon Multi-Object Rearrangement via Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions
talks.summary: DISCO (Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions) addresses long-horizon multi-object rearrangement by combining Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with policy learning. It utilizes progressive widening to search continuous action spaces and iterative distillation to improve policy performance without requiring search at test time.

subsections.title: Intro and Technical Delay
subsections.visual_caption: Session O6 title slide shown during a technical delay.
subsections.summary: The session chair introduces the final paper of the session, followed by a significant technical delay before the speaker begins.

subsections.title: Motivation: Search and Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram illustrating the combination of learning and search, inspired by AlphaGo.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the 'AlphaGo recipe' of combining search and learning, noting the challenges of applying this to robot manipulation due to continuous action spaces and long horizons.

subsections.title: Building a Search Tree with Progressive Widening
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of the search tree expansion using progressive widening.
subsections.summary: The method builds a search tree where nodes represent scene states and edges represent pick-and-place actions. Progressive widening is used to dynamically add new actions to the tree as nodes are visited more frequently.

subsections.title: Iterative Distillation
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing the iterative distillation loop between the search tree and the policy.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains the distillation process where search results are used to train a value function and fine-tune the policy, creating a self-improving loop that enhances long-horizon reasoning.

subsections.title: Conclusion and Results
subsections.visual_caption: Thank you slide featuring QR code and robot demos for shelf packing and table bussing.
subsections.summary: The talk concludes with results showing DISCO outperforming baselines in simulation and real-world rollouts for shelf packing and table bussing tasks.

subsections.title: Conclusion and Poster Invitation
subsections.visual_caption: Thank you slide with QR code and robot manipulation demos.
subsections.summary: The speaker concludes the presentation by highlighting the project website and inviting attendees to visit poster #176 for a challenge and rewards.

talks.session_title: Oral O7: Humanoid data, control and skills
talks.title: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models
talks.summary: GRAIL proposes a new paradigm for scaling robot learning by generating humanoid robot data from video world models instead of collecting it via teleoperation or motion capture. By using text prompts to generate natural human motions in diverse 3D scenes, the system can automatically produce large-scale, physically grounded datasets for training robust loco-manipulation policies.

subsections.title: Session O7 Introduction
subsections.visual_caption: Session O7 title slide: Humanoid data, control and skills.
subsections.summary: The session chair introduces the final oral session of the conference, focusing on humanoid robotics, and presents the first speaker from NVIDIA Research.

subsections.title: Motivation: Scaling Robot Learning
subsections.visual_caption: Title slide for GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models.
subsections.summary: Tianyu Xie introduces GRAIL and discusses the fundamental data problem in robotics, contrasting it with the abundance of data in other AI fields.

subsections.title: Session O7 Introduction
subsections.visual_caption: Session chair Koushil Sreenath introducing the final oral session.
subsections.summary: Session chair Koushil Sreenath introduces the final oral session of the conference, focusing on humanoid data, controls, and skills, featuring three papers including two best paper nominees.

subsections.title: The Robotics Data Problem
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of teleoperation and motion capture limitations vs. video world models.
subsections.summary: The speaker identifies the bottleneck in robotics as the slow and costly nature of data collection through teleoperation and motion capture, proposing video world models as a scalable alternative.

subsections.title: Generating Data from Video Models
subsections.visual_caption: Reconstructed human and object motions from generated video.
subsections.summary: The method uses text prompts to generate clean videos of human-object interactions, leveraging privileged 3D information from the generated scenes to reconstruct accurate motions for robot retargeting.

subsections.title: Grounding in Physics and Scaling
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of the 35,000+ physically valid motions generated by GRAIL.
subsections.summary: Kinematic motions are grounded in physics using a terrain-aware whole-body tracker, allowing the generation of over 35,000 physically valid motions covering diverse tasks like stair climbing and object carrying.

subsections.title: Sim-to-Real Results and Q&A
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world robot demos of object pickup and stair climbing.
subsections.summary: The trained policies demonstrate zero-shot transfer to real robots for object pickup and navigating unseen terrain. During Q&A, the speaker discusses how video models incorporate prior knowledge of object weight and the potential for direct humanoid video generation.

talks.session_title: Oral O7: Humanoid data, control and skills
talks.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
talks.summary: SuperMimic introduces a highly efficient framework for scaling humanoid whole-body control by utilizing a single differentiable world model to learn body dynamics. This approach reduces GPU training hours by three orders of magnitude compared to state-of-the-art methods while achieving higher returns and fewer failures across massive motion datasets.

subsections.title: Scaling Motion Tracking
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing 1000x reduction in GPU hours vs. SOTA.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights the 1000x reduction in compute requirements achieved by SuperMimic, addressing the bottleneck of 'burning GPUs' in large-scale motion tracking.

subsections.title: Learning Dynamics with One Model
subsections.visual_caption: Live demo of a robot catching itself in a browser-based world model.
subsections.summary: The core idea is to learn body dynamics once using a differentiable world model, which allows for efficient policy updates through backpropagation and imagination.

subsections.title: Training via Imagination
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of training time: 3 hours on 1 GPU vs. 7 days on 128 GPUs.
subsections.summary: By training in imagination rather than simulation, SuperMimic achieves significantly faster iteration cycles and higher returns with fewer training steps than standard PPO.

subsections.title: Generalization and Community Impact
subsections.visual_caption: Grid of diverse robot motions and community reproductions.
subsections.summary: The method generalizes to new bodies and sparse reward tasks. The speaker notes the rapid community adoption and open-sources the code during the talk.

subsections.title: Q&A: World Models vs. Simulators
subsections.visual_caption: Speaker answering questions about the world model architecture.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains that the differentiable world model is a simple three-layer MLP, making it much cheaper to run than a full differentiable simulator for backward passes.

talks.session_title: Oral O7: Humanoid data, control and skills
talks.title: RoboNaldo: Accurate, Stable and Powerful Humanoid Soccer Shooting via Motion-Guided Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
talks.summary: RoboNaldo presents a framework for accurate and powerful humanoid soccer shooting using a three-stage motion-guided curriculum reinforcement learning approach. The system integrates egocentric onboard perception with LiDAR and cameras to enable a Unitree G1 robot to approach and kick both stationary and moving balls with high precision and velocity in real-world environments.

subsections.title: The Challenge of Soccer Shooting
subsections.visual_caption: Unitree G1 robot attempting a soccer kick in a lab.
subsections.summary: The speaker outlines the three requirements for successful humanoid soccer: precision of contact, powerful force-aware impact, and stable recovery after the kick.

subsections.title: Three-Stage Curriculum RL
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the three-stage curriculum: motion tracking, stationary ball, and moving ball.
subsections.summary: The framework progresses from basic motion tracking to accurate ball interaction and finally unified locomotion, allowing the robot to approach the ball dynamically before shooting.

subsections.title: Egocentric Onboard Perception
subsections.visual_caption: LiDAR and camera setup for ball and target detection.
subsections.summary: The robot uses a down-tilted LiDAR to detect reflective balls and a chest camera for AprilTag target detection, enabling autonomous operation without external motion capture.

subsections.title: Real-Robot Experiments
subsections.visual_caption: Robot shooting soccer balls across diverse indoor and outdoor scenes.
subsections.summary: Experiments on the Unitree G1 show high success rates for both stationary and moving balls, achieving kick velocities up to 13.1 m/s, roughly 60% of a professional player's speed.

subsections.title: Future Work and Session Conclusion
subsections.visual_caption: Demos of extended skills like humanoid table tennis and manipulation.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses extending the system to other whole-body intelligence tasks like table tennis. The session concludes with a discussion on the timeline for robots playing soccer with humans.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Tuesday Early PM
talks.title: Building general purpose robots with Gemini
talks.summary: Kanishka Rao presents the Gemini Robotics team's approach to achieving generalized dexterity by combining high-level reasoning from frontier models with low-level whole-body control. The talk highlights the capabilities of Gemini Robotics 2.0 and 2.5, including room-scale tasks, multi-robot collaboration, and improved safety features.

subsections.title: Problem Motivation: General Reasoning vs. Dexterity
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing the bridge between Frontier Models and Robot Models to achieve Generalized Dexterity.
subsections.summary: The talk introduces the core challenge of combining high-level general reasoning with low-level dexterous whole-body control in robotics.

subsections.title: Gemini Robotics 2.0 and 2.5 Capabilities
subsections.visual_caption: Video demo of the Apollo humanoid performing room-scale tasks with whole-body control.
subsections.summary: Overview of the Gemini Robotics 2.0 and 2.5 releases, demonstrating room-scale manipulation, multi-finger hand control, and multi-robot collaboration.

subsections.title: Real-World Deployment and Safety
subsections.visual_caption: Performance metrics and real-world deployment demo at a Mercedes-Benz production line.
subsections.summary: Discussion of real-world performance at a Mercedes-Benz production line and the introduction of new safety and jailbreak-resistance benchmarks.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Tuesday Early PM
talks.title: Actions and Agents for True Long-Horizon Behavior
talks.summary: Alberto Rodriguez discusses Boston Dynamics' work on long-horizon behavior for the Atlas humanoid, focusing on logistics tasks like part sequencing. The talk details the system architecture, which separates high-level reasoning (Job Harness) from low-level physical control, and emphasizes the importance of data quality over data scale.

subsections.title: Atlas in Manufacturing: Sequencing Task
subsections.visual_caption: Video of Atlas performing a fully autonomous part sequencing task in a manufacturing environment.
subsections.summary: Introduction to the Atlas humanoid's deployment in a car manufacturing plant for logistics and part sequencing.

subsections.title: System Architecture: Reasoning and Action Models
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram showing the separation between System 2 (Job Harness/Reasoning) and System 1 (Action Model).
subsections.summary: Detailed breakdown of the two-system architecture, where a high-level reasoning model (Job Harness) orchestrates the low-level physical action model.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Tuesday Early PM
talks.title: The Reference Platform for Physical AI
talks.summary: Sven Parusel, Head of Research Partnerships at Agile Robots and Co-Founder of Franka Robotics, presents their vision for a reference platform for physical AI. He discusses the evolution of the Franka Research 3 (FR3) arm, the introduction of the FR3 Duo dual-arm system, and the release of the LABS open-source software suite for teleoperation and data collection.

subsections.title: Introduction to Franka Robotics
subsections.visual_caption: Franka Robotics company overview
subsections.summary: Sven provides an overview of Franka Robotics, its research-driven roots at DLR, and its current role within Agile Robots.

subsections.title: Franka Research 3 (FR3)
subsections.visual_caption: Franka Research 3 arm specifications
subsections.summary: A deep dive into the FR3 arm, highlighting its torque sensing capabilities and its status as a backbone for robotics learning research.

subsections.title: FR3 Duo and Mobile Platforms
subsections.visual_caption: FR3 Duo dual-arm system
subsections.summary: Introduction of the FR3 Duo, a dual-arm system designed for physical AI research, and its mobile counterpart for whole-body manipulation.

subsections.title: Franka Robotics Mission and Research 3 Platform
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing the specifications of the Franka Research 3 arm.
subsections.summary: Overview of Franka Robotics' mission to provide open research platforms and the technical specifications of the Franka Research 3 arm.

subsections.title: LABS: Teleoperation & Data Collection
subsections.visual_caption: LABS open-source software suite
subsections.summary: Presentation of the LABS suite, an open-source pipeline designed to streamline teleoperation, data collection, and model training for the robotics community.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: DeTac: Dual-branch Decoupling of Texture and Force Signals in Vision-Based Tactile Sensors
talks.affiliation: Peking University, AI Robotics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
talks.summary: DeTac is a dual-branch generative framework that decouples texture and force signals in vision-based tactile sensors. It uses a shading restoration branch and a marker extraction branch with cross-branch synergistic optimization to improve tactile sensing accuracy.

subsections.title: Problem & Motivation
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the DeTac framework and the limitations of existing serial pipelines.
subsections.summary: The authors identify that existing vision-based tactile sensors couple texture and force signals, and current serial data-driven methods suffer from mask-sizing dilemmas and error retention.

subsections.title: Core Architecture & Method
subsections.visual_caption: The DeTac dual-branch architecture diagram.
subsections.summary: DeTac uses a dual-branch architecture with a shading restoration branch and a marker extraction branch, optimized by cross-branch synergistic losses to decouple the signals.

subsections.title: Experiments & Results
subsections.visual_caption: Qualitative comparison of shading restoration and marker extraction results.
subsections.summary: Experiments show that DeTac produces more natural shading restoration and precise marker extraction, leading to improved performance in real-world fabric classification tasks.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: FingerEye: Learning Dexterous Manipulation with Continuous Vision-Tactile Sensing
talks.affiliation: National University of Singapore, RoboScience, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, South China University of Technology
talks.summary: FingerEye is a vision-tactile fingertip sensor designed for dexterous manipulation. It uses two cameras to provide continuous vision-tactile sensing, enabling robust contact tracking and improved performance in contact-rich tasks.

subsections.title: Motivation & Sensor Design
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of FingerEye with existing see-through skin sensors.
subsections.summary: The authors introduce FingerEye, a compact fingertip sensor with two cameras that provides continuous vision-tactile feedback, addressing limitations of existing see-through skin sensors.

subsections.title: Learning & Experiments
subsections.visual_caption: Performance comparison showing FingerEye improves success rates.
subsections.summary: The authors demonstrate that FingerEye improves success rates in dexterous manipulation tasks by providing continuous vision-tactile feedback and using a group-structured fusion policy.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: DAVATaR: Depth-Aware Visually Augmented Tactile Learning Across the Air-Water Interface
talks.summary: DAVATaR is a framework for submerged manipulation that uses fluidically innervated tactile sensing and visual augmentation to handle the challenges of the air-water interface, such as refraction and glare.

subsections.title: Challenges in Submerged Manipulation
subsections.visual_caption: Visual challenges in submerged manipulation: reflection, waves, turbidity, and refraction.
subsections.summary: The authors highlight the challenges of submerged manipulation, including visual distortions at the air-water interface and the need to protect tactile electronics from water.

subsections.title: DAVATaR Framework
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the DAVATaR framework components.
subsections.summary: DAVATaR uses fluidically innervated tactile sensing to keep electronics dry and visual augmentation to handle refraction and glare, significantly improving success rates in submerged tasks.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: Visible Touch: Rendering Contact for Visuomotor Policies
talks.summary: Visible Touch is a method that projects magnetic tactile sensor readings as visual overlays into camera images, allowing pre-trained vision-based policies to learn from contact information without architectural changes.

subsections.title: Motivation & Method
subsections.visual_caption: The Visible Touch method: projecting tactile readings as visual arrows.
subsections.summary: The authors propose Visible Touch, which projects magnetic tactile sensor readings as visual arrows into camera images, enabling pre-trained vision-based policies to incorporate contact information.

subsections.title: Experiments & Results
subsections.visual_caption: Performance comparison showing Visible Touch improves success rates.
subsections.summary: Experiments demonstrate that Visible Touch significantly improves success rates in contact-rich manipulation tasks across both simulation and real-world settings.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: Demystifying When and Why VLAs Fail in Contact-Rich Tasks and How to Fix Them
talks.summary: This work analyzes why Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models fail in contact-rich tasks, identifying precision and force failures, and proposes fixes using logit-normal noise scheduling and time-aware force injection.

subsections.title: Failure Analysis
subsections.visual_caption: Identification of precision and force failures in VLA models.
subsections.summary: The authors identify two main failure modes in VLA models for contact-rich tasks: precision failures during alignment and force failures in identifying when a task is complete.

subsections.title: Proposed Fixes & Results
subsections.visual_caption: Performance improvements using logit-normal noise and time-aware force injection.
subsections.summary: The authors propose using logit-normal noise scheduling to improve precision and time-aware force injection to handle contact dynamics, leading to significant success rate improvements.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection
talks.affiliation: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai Innovation Institute, Southern University of Science and Technology, Noematrix
talks.summary: This work introduces LIFT, a method to add force awareness to pre-trained VLA models using a reactive action expert and force memory, improving performance in contact-rich tasks without full retraining.

subsections.title: Motivation & Method
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the LIFT framework with reactive action expert.
subsections.summary: The authors propose LIFT, which adds a reactive action expert and force memory to pre-trained VLA models, enabling them to respond to force feedback in contact-rich tasks.

subsections.title: Experiments & Results
subsections.visual_caption: Performance comparison showing LIFT improves success rates.
subsections.summary: Experiments show that LIFT improves contact adaptation and success rates in various manipulation tasks by enabling reactive force responses.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: Combining Constrained Sampling and Reinforcement Learning for Manipulation
talks.summary: This work addresses the exploration problem in reinforcement learning for manipulation by defining a constrained manifold based on first principles of physics. By sampling from this manifold, the method can guide RL using reset sampling and curricula to train policies for complex tasks like dexterous in-hand manipulation.

subsections.title: Problem & Motivation
subsections.visual_caption: The exploration bottleneck in reinforcement learning for manipulation.
subsections.summary: The authors identify exploration as the core bottleneck in reinforcement learning for manipulation and propose using constrained sampling to guide the learning process.

subsections.title: Constrained Sampling Method
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the constrained sampling method.
subsections.summary: The authors use first principles to define a constraint manifold and sample from it to guide reinforcement learning, significantly improving exploration and task success.

subsections.title: Constrained Sampling from First Principles
subsections.visual_caption: Equations defining the constrained manifold based on contact complementarities and friction cones.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains how physics principles like contact modes and friction cones can define a constrained manifold of physically feasible states for manipulation.

subsections.title: RL Guided by Constrained Samples
subsections.visual_caption: Robot hand performing dexterous in-hand cube manipulation using constrained sampling.
subsections.summary: The talk demonstrates how constrained sampling enables training for complex tasks like balancing a cube on fingertips, where naive exploration would fail.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S4: Touch, force and contact-rich manipulation
talks.title: TAM: Torque Adaptation Module for Robust Motion Transfer in Manipulation
talks.affiliation: KAIST, Allen Institute for AI, University of Toronto, University of Washington
talks.summary: TAM is a torque adaptation module that corrects robot-side torque based on recent motion history, enabling robust motion transfer across different robot dynamics and payloads without policy retraining.

subsections.title: Motivation & Method
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the TAM framework.
subsections.summary: The authors introduce TAM, a module that adapts torque commands based on motion history to handle variations in robot dynamics and payloads.

subsections.title: Experiments & Results
subsections.visual_caption: Performance comparison showing TAM improves success rates.
subsections.summary: Experiments demonstrate that TAM enables robust motion transfer across different robot instances and payloads, significantly improving success rates in manipulation tasks.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: Learning Physics-Guided Residual Dynamics for Deformable Object Simulation
talks.summary: PGRD combines physics-based simulation with learning-based residuals to accurately predict the dynamics of deformable objects. This hybrid approach enables robots to plan manipulation strategies for heterogeneous objects like ropes and dusters, outperforming pure physics or pure learning baselines.

subsections.title: Physics-Guided Residual Dynamics (PGRD) Framework
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the PGRD pipeline combining physics simulation and neural network residuals.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces PGRD, which extracts particle data from RGBD observations and uses a neural network to predict residuals on top of physics-based state predictions.

subsections.title: Simulation Results and Task Execution
subsections.visual_caption: Robot executing a rope rerouting task using PGRD simulation and MPPI.
subsections.summary: The method is validated on rope and duster objects, showing superior accuracy in modeling heterogeneous dynamics and enabling automated task execution via natural language goals.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: WireCraft: A Simulation Benchmark for Industrial DLO Manipulation
talks.summary: WireCraft is a shared simulation benchmark for industrial wire manipulation, featuring tasks like connector insertion, clip routing, and channel seating. The benchmark provides diverse wire models and randomization to test policy generalization, demonstrating significant success in sim-to-real transfer on a physical UR5 robot.

subsections.title: WireCraft Benchmark Tasks
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the three core tasks in WireCraft: connector insertion, clip routing, and channel seating.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces WireCraft to address the lack of standardized benchmarks in wire manipulation, detailing its configurable tasks and randomized environments.

subsections.title: Sim-to-Real Validation
subsections.visual_caption: Physical UR5 robot performing wire insertion tasks validated against simulation data.
subsections.summary: Results show that mixing simulation data with real demonstrations improves insertion success rates from 15% to 80%, proving the benchmark's utility for real-world robotics.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: Enabling Robust Cloth Manipulation via Inference-Time Simulator-in-the-Loop Refinement
talks.summary: This work proposes using a fast, faithful simulator (FLASH) as an inference-time forward model to refine cloth manipulation policies. By combining real-to-sim state recovery with MPPI-based refinement, the system achieves high success rates on complex folding tasks and robustly recovers from external disturbances.

subsections.title: Simulator-in-the-Loop Framework
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the proposed framework including FLASH simulator and MPPI refinement.
subsections.summary: The speaker describes a pipeline where RGB images are converted to cloth meshes and refined via parallel rollouts in the FLASH simulator using MPPI.

subsections.title: Real-World Evaluation and Robustness
subsections.visual_caption: Real robot performing single and dual-arm cloth folding tasks.
subsections.summary: The system achieves 90% success on single-arm folds and demonstrates robustness by recovering from mid-fold disturbances eight out of ten times.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: Robustness without Wrinkles: Parallel Simulation and Robust MPC for Certified Deformable Manipulation
talks.summary: CORD-SLS is a framework for deformable object manipulation that provides differentiable simulation and GPU-accelerated robust output feedback control. By smoothing contact dynamics and using conformal prediction for error bounds, it enables safe, real-time manipulation of high-dimensional objects like ropes and cloth.

subsections.title: CORD-SLS Framework and Differentiable Simulation
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the CORD-SLS framework for contact-smoothed robust control.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces CORD-SLS, which uses implicit differentiation and smooth surrogate functions to provide useful gradients for optimizing high-dimensional deformable dynamics.

subsections.title: Robust Control and Hardware Validation
subsections.visual_caption: Hardware experiments showing rope manipulation and cloth folding with obstacle avoidance.
subsections.summary: The framework is validated on hardware, demonstrating zero obstacle collisions during rope manipulation and successful high-dimensional cloth folding using robust state feedback.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: Noise-Invariant Spatial Encoding for 3D Manipulation Policies under Depth Corruption
talks.summary: NISE (Noise-Invariant Spatial Encoding) addresses the unreliability of depth observations for transparent and reflective objects in 3D manipulation. By using cross-view supervision and uncertainty-aware attention, NISE learns robust spatial features that maintain high success rates even under severe depth corruption.

subsections.title: NISE: Robust Spatial Encoding
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture of NISE showing cross-view supervision and Gaussian Marginalized 3D Attention.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains how NISE uses cross-view consistency and marginalized attention to down-weight unreliable depth data while preserving useful geometric features.

subsections.title: Performance under Depth Noise
subsections.visual_caption: Real robot experiments collecting reflective gears and handling transparent test tubes.
subsections.summary: NISE significantly outperforms baselines in both simulation and real-world tasks involving transparent and reflective objects, maintaining robustness as depth noise increases.

subsections.title: Method Summary
subsections.visual_caption: NISE: Trustworthy Spatial Encoding From Imperfect Depth.
subsections.summary: Summary of NISE's ability to learn spatial features that remain useful when depth is unreliable through cross-view supervision and uncertainty-aware attention.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: SERF: Spatiotemporal Environment and Robot Feature Map for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
talks.summary: SERF proposes a spatiotemporal environment and robot feature map that enables long-horizon reasoning for mobile manipulation tasks by explicitly accumulating information over time.

subsections.title: Motivation & Problem
subsections.visual_caption: SERF: Spatiotemporal Environment and Robot Feature Map for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the limitations of current robot foundation models in handling spatially and temporally extended tasks due to implicit context encoding.

subsections.title: Spatiotemporal Feature Map
subsections.visual_caption: Map-conditioned VLA Policy.
subsections.summary: Explanation of the SERF map representation using neural points for the scene and robot body, updated online using egocentric observations.

subsections.title: Experimental Results
subsections.visual_caption: Experiments on Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation.
subsections.summary: Evaluation of the map-conditioned policy on long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks, showing improved robustness and faster subgoal reaching.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: Articulated 3D Scene Graphs for Open-World Mobile Manipulation
talks.summary: MoMa-SG is a scalable method for understanding articulation kinematics and object-level semantics in open-world environments, enabling robots to interact with complex household objects.

subsections.title: Introduction to Articulated Objects
subsections.visual_caption: Articulated 3D Scene Graphs for Open-World Mobile Manipulation.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces the challenge of interacting with articulated objects like fridges and drawers in everyday home environments.

subsections.title: MoMa-SG Methodology
subsections.visual_caption: MoMa-SG - Method.
subsections.summary: Overview of the MoMa-SG method, including interaction discovery, articulation estimation, and open-vocabulary 3D part mapping.

subsections.title: Real-World Manipulation Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Results - Articulated 3D Scene Graphs.
subsections.summary: Demonstration of MoMa-SG as a backbone for long-horizon mobile manipulation using a Toyota HSR and a Boston Dynamics Spot robot.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: RAM: Reachability Across Morphologies
talks.summary: RAM is a model that predicts reachability across different robot morphologies in nanoseconds, significantly accelerating morphology optimization for workspace coverage and trajectory following.

subsections.title: Reachability Challenges
subsections.visual_caption: RAM: Reachability Across Morphologies.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains the computational expense of solving inverse kinematics for arbitrary morphologies and the need for fast reachability queries.

subsections.title: RAM Architecture & Dataset
subsections.visual_caption: 30,000,000,000 Samples across 30,000 Morphologies.
subsections.summary: Description of the RAM architecture, consisting of an occupancy network and an encoder, trained on a massive dataset of 30 billion samples.

subsections.title: Morphology Optimization
subsections.visual_caption: Gradients through RAM, not IK.
subsections.summary: Demonstration of using RAM's differentiability to optimize robot morphologies for reachability by backpropagating through the model.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S5: Deformable manipulation, geometry and morphology
talks.title: Shape Your Body: Value Gradients for Multi-Embodiment Robot Design
talks.summary: Shape Your Body presents a data-driven approach to robot hardware design using value gradients from a multi-embodiment critic to optimize thousands of design parameters simultaneously.

subsections.title: Data-Driven Robot Design
subsections.visual_caption: Shape Your Body: Value Gradients for Multi-Embodiment Robot Design.
subsections.summary: The speaker proposes using deep learning to automate robot hardware design, similar to how it has revolutionized robotics control.

subsections.title: Value Gradient Optimization
subsections.visual_caption: Robots learn behavior from data. Robot design is still done by hand.
subsections.summary: Explanation of the Value Gradient Design Search (VGDS) method, which uses a frozen critic to optimize embodiment parameters across various robot types.

talks.session_title: Keynote II — Russ Tedrake
talks.title: Learning in the factories
talks.summary: Russ Tedrake discusses the scaling of robot learning from one-to-one human supervision to large-scale autonomous fleets in manufacturing. He emphasizes the value of deployment data, the role of foundation models in reducing the need for mid-training data, and the importance of 'jidoka' (automation with a human touch) for efficient error handling and root-cause analysis.
talks.official_abstract: How do we make large models for manipulation useful in real applications, and what value can real-world deployments bring back to the models? Sharing lessons from deploying Walden Robotics manipulation systems into live factory production environments and how performance scales with real-world deployment.
talks.speaker_bio: Russ Tedrake is co-founder and CEO of Walden Robotics and Toyota Professor of EECS, AeroAstro, and Mechanical Engineering at MIT, formerly SVP of Large Behavior Models at Toyota Research Institute.

subsections.title: Introduction and Speaker Bio
subsections.visual_caption: Ani Majumdar introducing Russ Tedrake
subsections.summary: Ani Majumdar introduces Russ Tedrake, highlighting his research trajectory from early robot learning to model-based control and back to large-scale learning models.

subsections.title: The Rocket Ship of Robotics
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: 'Dude, did you see that OpenAI just solved robotics?!'
subsections.summary: Russ discusses the current 'rocket ship' moment in robotics, addressing the angst caused by rapid progress in foundation models and the need to bridge business deployment with rigorous research.

subsections.title: Walden Robotics: Full-Stack Deployment
subsections.visual_caption: Walden Robotics 101 slide showing humanoid robots
subsections.summary: Introduction to Walden Robotics, a spin-out from Toyota Research Institute, focusing on full-stack integration and getting robots out of the lab and into the field.

subsections.title: Core Beliefs for Real-World Impact
subsections.visual_caption: Slide outlining core beliefs: Technology is ready, Full stack is needed, Field data is most valuable
subsections.summary: Russ outlines his core convictions: that the technology is ready for scale, that companies must be full-stack to meet production requirements, and that field data is the most valuable resource.

subsections.title: The Human Element on the Factory Floor
subsections.visual_caption: Video of a Walden robot loading camshafts in a factory
subsections.summary: A discussion on the social impact of deploying humanoid robots, emphasizing the importance of empathy and the 'boring' initial deployment to build trust with factory workers.

subsections.title: Case Study: 33,000 Camshafts
subsections.visual_caption: Robot performing a complex handover of a heavy camshaft
subsections.summary: Russ details their first major deployment loading camshafts for Toyota, explaining why this ergonomically difficult task was chosen and the high stakes of production-line reliability.

subsections.title: Shared Autonomy and HG-Dagger
subsections.visual_caption: Remote assistance interface showing robot-eye view and human intervention
subsections.summary: Explanation of the shared autonomy approach using a variant of HG-Dagger, where remote human assistance ensures 100% success rates while collecting critical intervention data.

subsections.title: Scaling Laws and Model Improvement
subsections.visual_caption: Plot showing Mean Time Between Interventions (MTBI) improving over deployment weeks
subsections.summary: Russ presents data showing how their Large Behavior Models (LBM) improve over time through iterative training on deployment data, reaching a breakthrough in autonomy.

subsections.title: Zero-Shot Capabilities and Emergent Skills
subsections.visual_caption: Robot unscrewing a bottle cap in a kitchen environment
subsections.summary: Demonstration of the model's zero-shot capabilities in non-factory tasks, showing emergent skills like active vision and complex manipulation from large-scale pre-training.

subsections.title: The Value of Deployment Data
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: 'How Much is Robot Deployment Data Worth?'
subsections.summary: A deep dive into the 'data flywheel' argument, discussing why stronger base models actually learn more effectively from the sparse intervention data provided by field deployments.

subsections.title: Core Beliefs at Walden Robotics
subsections.visual_caption: Slide listing core beliefs about base models and deployment data.
subsections.summary: The speaker outlines core beliefs including the commoditization of mid-training data and the increasing value of deployment data as base models strengthen.

subsections.title: Scaling Beyond HG-Dagger
subsections.visual_caption: Robot hardware demo of a runtime monitor asking for remote assistance.
subsections.summary: Discussion on moving from 1:1 operation to many-to-one by implementing runtime monitoring where policies autonomously ask for human help when stuck.

subsections.title: Learning from Toyota: Jidoka and the 5 Whys
subsections.visual_caption: Historical photo of a Toyota loom factory illustrating Jidoka.
subsections.summary: Russ connects modern AI remote assistance to the Toyota principle of Jidoka, emphasizing the importance of stopping the line to perform root-cause analysis using the '5 Whys'.

subsections.title: The Manufacturing Bottleneck
subsections.visual_caption: Video of robots being used to assemble other robots.
subsections.summary: The primary bottleneck is identified as the physical manufacturing of robots at scale, which Walden addresses by using robots to build robots and partnering with mass-production experts like Toyota.

subsections.title: Summary and Key Points
subsections.visual_caption: Summary slide with key takeaways and Walden Robotics contact info.
subsections.summary: Final wrap-up emphasizing that deployment data is the most valuable asset and that the field must learn from the masterful experience of mass production in factories.

subsections.title: Q&A: Academia's Role and Success Metrics
subsections.visual_caption: Russ Tedrake taking questions from the audience.
subsections.summary: Russ answers questions regarding academia's contribution to intervention data research, the difficulty of verifying task completion visually, and the compute/data requirements for startups.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Tuesday Late PM
talks.title: Meta Robotics Studio: Building an Autonomous Humanoid for the Home
talks.summary: Jonathan Tompson presents Meta's foundational technologies for robotics, including SLAM, hand tracking, and egocentric data collection via Aria glasses. He discusses their work on generalized dexterous foundation models and the use of the SuperDex simulator for high-fidelity physics simulation.

subsections.title: Meta Robotics Studio Mission
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: Building a home robot takes a multidisciplinary team.
subsections.summary: Introduction to the team's goal of creating a useful and delightful humanoid for household tasks and social interaction.

subsections.title: Challenges of Bipedal Robots in the Home
subsections.visual_caption: Slide detailing the foundations positioning Meta to succeed in home robotics.
subsections.summary: Jonathan explains why the home is a difficult environment for robots due to unpredictability (kids, pets) and the high precision required for bipedal manipulation.

subsections.title: Foundational Technologies at Meta
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: Our foundations position Meta to succeed
subsections.summary: Overview of Meta's core technologies including SLAM, hand tracking, Aria egocentric data, and vision models like SAM 3.

subsections.title: Generalized Dexterous Foundation Models
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: Meta is building generalized, dexterous robot foundation models
subsections.summary: Discussion on building VLA models using human priors, simulation, and large-scale data collection from human egocentric video and robot teleoperation.

subsections.title: Aria and SLAM Infrastructure
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: Aria unlocks egocentric data, for us and our partners
subsections.summary: Details on the Aria wearable glasses for eye tracking and millimeter-precision SLAM, and leveraging Quest headset infrastructure for robotics.

subsections.title: Simulation and Frontier Models
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: Muse plans the task, and a Muse-based policy turns the plan into motion
subsections.summary: Introduction of SuperDex for FEM simulation of non-rigid objects and the use of Muse frontier models for agentic task planning and code generation.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Tuesday Late PM
talks.title: Scaling Robot Intelligence: From Human Experience to Self-Improving Robots
talks.summary: Yongjian Shen presents AGIBOT's physical AI ecosystem, highlighting their large-scale robot deployment and open-source datasets. He introduces the GO-3 world reasoning action model and demonstrates collective experience learning across a fleet of 96 robots.

subsections.title: AGIBOT Robot Deployment and Ecosystem
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: AGIBOT: More Than Robot Manufacturing
subsections.summary: Overview of AGIBOT's production of over 20,000 robots and their deployment in factories and public infrastructure like the Guangzhou Metro.

subsections.title: AGIBOT WORLD Dataset and Reasoning
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: AGIBOT WORLD 2024 and 2026
subsections.summary: Introduction of the open-source dataset containing over 1 million trajectories and human experience data for model training.

subsections.title: GO-3 World Reasoning Action Model
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: GO-3 Preview: World Reasoning Action Model
subsections.summary: Technical details of the GO-3 model which connects reasoning, future state prediction, and action generation for complex tasks.

subsections.title: Collective Experience Learning (CEL)
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: Genie Master: Learning from Deployment
subsections.summary: Demonstration of 96 robots learning simultaneously in real-world manipulation tasks and the Genie Master system for deployment-based evolution.

subsections.title: RoboColiseum Benchmark
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: RoboColiseum: Benchmarking the Core Capabilities of Robot Models
subsections.summary: Introduction of a community-driven benchmark for instruction following, spatial reasoning, and general manipulation with a focus on closing the sim-to-real gap.

talks.session_title: Diamond Sponsor Talks — Tuesday Late PM
talks.title: Building Foundational Models for Robotics at Tesla
talks.summary: Patrick Cho discusses Tesla's approach to building robust policies for both autonomous driving (Cybercab) and humanoid robotics (Optimus) using world models. He emphasizes the importance of evaluating counterfactuals and training in physically accurate simulations to handle rare tail-end scenarios.

subsections.title: Motivation for Robust Policies
subsections.visual_caption: Video: Motivating Example of a person throwing a rock at a robot taxi
subsections.summary: Discussion on the necessity of robust policies for public trust, using real-world edge cases like road interference and unexpected obstacles.

subsections.title: World Models for Counterfactual Evaluation
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: World Models Characteristics
subsections.summary: Explaining the three motivations for world models: counterfactual evaluation (what if no intervention?), testing new policies, and large-scale training.

subsections.title: Characteristics of Effective World Models
subsections.visual_caption: Slide: World Models Characteristics (Causal, Interactive, Consistent, Low Latency, Physically Accurate)
subsections.summary: Defining the five key requirements for world models to be useful for robot policy training and evaluation.

subsections.title: Simulating Tail-End Scenarios
subsections.visual_caption: Video: Generated frames showing a tree branch falling and an elephant crossing the road
subsections.summary: Demonstrating the power of generative world models to create rare scenarios, such as falling trees or animals on the road, to test policy reactions in a safe environment.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: RoboKit: Accelerating Parallel Differentiable Optimization for Robot Learning
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 105
talks.summary: RoboKit is a framework designed to accelerate parallel differentiable optimization for robot learning tasks. It supports diverse tasks from inverse kinematics to motion planning and grasping, achieving significant speedups (up to 16x) over existing baselines by leveraging GPU parallelism and hybrid geometry structures.

subsections.title: Optimization with Analytical Objectives and Simulation
subsections.visual_caption: RoboKit components: Objectives, Optimizers, and Acceleration.
subsections.summary: The presenter introduces RoboKit's support for analytical Jacobians and its ability to apply cost functions to rollouts using Model Predictive Control (MPC).

subsections.title: Benchmarks and Scaling
subsections.visual_caption: Speed benchmarks across various tasks compared to baselines.
subsections.summary: RoboKit demonstrates 10x to 68x speed improvements over baselines like PyRoboKit and EasyHEC, scaling to solve thousands of IK problems in milliseconds.

subsections.title: Optimization vs. Neural Methods
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of optimization and neural-based methods.
subsections.summary: The talk concludes by identifying where neural methods provide advantages over pure optimization, specifically in handling complex physics, partial inputs, and inference speed.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: Control-Ready Uncertainty for Trajectory Diffusion
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 102
talks.summary: This work introduces SCOPE, a method to extract aleatoric uncertainty from trajectory diffusion models for real-time control. By leveraging the insight that diffusion scores encode log-density curvature, the method provides control-ready uncertainty tubes without the need for extensive sampling.

subsections.title: Motivation: Uncertainty in Diffusion Models
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of pedestrian and robot trajectory uncertainty.
subsections.summary: The speaker explains the need for robots to plan around uncertainty, noting that while diffusion models capture multi-modal distributions, the uncertainty remains implicit and slow to compute.

subsections.title: Key Insight: Curvature and Aleatoric Uncertainty
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing how score curvature is converted into uncertainty tubes.
subsections.summary: The core technical contribution is SCOPE, which converts diffusion score curvature into uncertainty tubes, enabling efficient training and fast test-time inference.

subsections.title: Control with SCOPE and Real-Robot Manipulation
subsections.visual_caption: Real-robot tomato picking task using SCOPE as a policy prior.
subsections.summary: The method is integrated into MPPI as a policy prior and forecast, demonstrating improved collision avoidance in real-robot manipulation tasks.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: Emergent Control via Prior-Based Free Energy Minimization
talks.affiliation: Infosys Center for Emerging Technology Solutions, India
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 72
talks.summary: Inspired by the free energy principle, this research proposes a method for emergent control by minimizing variational free energy based on goal-state priors. The approach provides a principled alternative to reward-based learning, demonstrating robust performance across diverse reinforcement learning environments.

subsections.title: Free Energy Principle and Gaussian Assumption
subsections.visual_caption: Schematic of the generative model and free energy minimization process.
subsections.summary: The talk introduces the free energy principle as a theory of neural function and explains how goal states are specified as priors to minimize squared distance from current states.

subsections.title: Task Performance: MountainCar, Highway, Walker, GoalReach
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of FE Agent and PPO in the highway driving environment.
subsections.summary: The method is evaluated across four tasks, showing smooth, collision-averse behavior in driving and steady locomotion in walking tasks compared to standard RL agents.

subsections.title: Comparison with Reward Shaping and Robustness to Noise
subsections.visual_caption: Optimization landscape comparison between unshaped reward and free energy.
subsections.summary: The presenters demonstrate that their method is task-structure agnostic and provides a richer optimization landscape and better robustness to noise than conventional RL models.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: GaP: A Graph-as-Policy Multi-Agent Self-Learning Harness For Variational Automation Tasks
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 100
talks.summary: Graph-as-Policy (GaP) is an agentic robotics framework that structures robot code as computation graphs generated by LLM agents. It enables autonomous self-learning through simulation rehearsal and real-to-sim-to-real refinement, achieving high success rates on variational automation tasks.

subsections.title: Variational Automation and Computation Graphs
subsections.visual_caption: Multi-agent harness architecture for perception, grasping, and planning.
subsections.summary: The speakers address the complexity of robot code in variational automation by structuring it as interpretable computation graphs generated by multiple LLM agents.

subsections.title: Self-Learning through Simulation Rehearsal
subsections.visual_caption: Case study of flipping heterogeneous objects in simulation.
subsections.summary: GaP allows agents to autonomously refine policies in simulation, demonstrating high robustness across diverse object geometries in tasks like flipping objects.

subsections.title: Agentic Real2Sim2Real and Benchmark Results
subsections.visual_caption: Simulation of sponge deformation for a metal bar wiping task.
subsections.summary: The framework supports real-to-sim-to-real refinement using smartphone video to improve simulation accuracy and graph structure, validated across eight benchmark tasks.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 99
talks.summary: RATs (Playful Agentic Robot Learning) enables robots to learn reusable code skills through self-directed play in simulation before receiving specific tasks.
