This 'play-time' experience builds a skill library that significantly improves success rates on novel, externally specified manipulation tasks.

subsections.title: Play-time Learning and Test-time Reuse
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of play-time learning and test-time skill reuse.
subsections.summary: The presenters describe how robots practice unfamiliar interactions in simulation to build a library of recallable skills, such as drawer pulling and grasp selection.

subsections.title: Benchmark Results: LIBERO-Pro and MoMoSpaces
subsections.visual_caption: Success rate improvements on MoMoSpaces benchmark.
subsections.summary: The RATs system shows significant success rate improvements (up to 20.6 percentage points) on held-out tasks across everyday interaction benchmarks.

subsections.title: Real-Robot Reuse and Conclusion
subsections.visual_caption: Real-robot cube swapping task using learned routines.
subsections.summary: The learned skill library is successfully transferred to a real robot for a cube swapping task without additional fine-tuning, demonstrating the power of self-directed play.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: Meta-Ctrl: Guaranteed Plan Generation by Decoupling Syntactic and Semantic Constraints
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 104
talks.summary: Meta-Ctrl ensures that LLM-generated robot plans follow task rules by decoupling syntactic and semantic constraints. By using meta-tokens to represent actions and performing a backward pass to compute the probability of reaching a goal, the method guarantees valid plan generation for complex tasks.

subsections.title: Decoupling Syntactic and Semantic Constraints
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of simple masking vs. looking ahead to the goal.
subsections.summary: The speakers explain how standard masking fails to ensure long-horizon goal reachability and introduce a chain-based state model to compute the chance of success.

subsections.title: Meta-Token Optimization for Efficiency
subsections.visual_caption: Efficiency comparison between token-level and action-level tracking.
subsections.summary: To handle the massive state space of JSON tokens, Meta-Ctrl tracks syntax and semantics at the action level using meta-tokens, drastically reducing memory requirements.

subsections.title: VirtualHome and Real-Robot Results
subsections.visual_caption: Real-robot dishwasher task comparison between baseline and Meta-Ctrl.
subsections.summary: Meta-Ctrl improves Llama 3B success rates from 20% to 90% on VirtualHome and achieves 100% valid plans in real-robot experiments by enforcing preconditions.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: Bayesian Active Learning for Intent Disambiguation in Interactive Robot Planning
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 103
talks.summary: This research presents a Bayesian active learning framework for disambiguating user intent in interactive robot planning. By using temporal logic as a shared task representation, the system generates informative clarification questions and converts the resolved intent into feasible, safe robot trajectories.

subsections.title: Intent Disambiguation in Human-Robot Interaction
subsections.visual_caption: Example of an ambiguous instruction in a multi-tank environment.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights the problem of ambiguous natural language instructions and the limitations of standard LLM-generated clarification questions.

subsections.title: Shared Task Representation with Temporal Logic
subsections.visual_caption: Temporal logic (STL) representation for task constraints.
subsections.summary: The framework uses Signal Temporal Logic (STL) to connect intent clarification with downstream planning, allowing the robot to reason about order and constraints.

subsections.title: Active Learning and Factory Inspection Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Quadruped robot performing equipment inspection in a factory.
subsections.summary: The system is evaluated in a complex factory environment, showing improved task success with fewer user questions by explicitly modeling intent uncertainty.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S6: Optimization, agentic planning and evaluation
talks.title: ATOM-Bench: A Real-World Benchmark for Atomic Skills and Compositional Generalization in Manipulation Policies
talks.affiliation: Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Peking University
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 107
talks.summary: ATOM-Bench is a real-world benchmark designed to evaluate atomic skills and compositional generalization in robot manipulation policies. It decomposes complex tasks into motor and instruction atoms, providing a diagnostic framework to identify whether failures stem from motor control, language grounding, or skill composition.

subsections.title: Motivation: Why Manipulation Policies Fail
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the ATOM-Bench framework and evaluation tracks.
subsections.summary: The presenter explains that single success rates don't reveal why policies fail, necessitating a benchmark that evaluates individual skills and their recombination.

subsections.title: Atomic Skill Library and Multi-Task Fine-Tuning
subsections.visual_caption: Definitions of motor atoms and instruction atoms.
subsections.summary: The benchmark defines six motor atoms (e.g., reorient, pour) and seven instruction atoms (e.g., color, count) to test physical execution and language grounding.

subsections.title: Compositional Generalization and Failure Analysis
subsections.visual_caption: Failure case examples related to motor execution and reference understanding.
subsections.summary: Evaluation of five SOTA policies shows that while atomic skills are improving, compositional generalization remains a significant challenge for current models.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: Kamino: GPU-based Simulation of Rigid Multi-Body Physics with Kinematic Loops
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 98
talks.summary: Introduces Kamino, a GPU-based physics solver for rigid multi-body systems with kinematic loops. It addresses numerical ill-conditioning in complex systems like Disney's audio-animatronic figures. Results show high-accuracy simulation of thousands of worlds simultaneously, facilitating reinforcement learning for control.

subsections.title: Motivation: Audio-Animatronics Figures
subsections.visual_caption: Olaf Audio-Animatronics figure demo.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces Disney's goal of bringing characters to life as accurate-to-scale robotic systems, which require simulating hundreds of bodies and joints.

subsections.title: Kamino Physics Solver
subsections.visual_caption: Numerical challenges slide showing kinematic loops.
subsections.summary: Kamino is introduced as a physics solver within Newton that handles kinematic loops, multi-contact coupling, and large mass ratios using a constrained maximal coordinate dynamics formulation.

subsections.title: Validation & Demo Systems
subsections.visual_caption: Dr. Legs bipedal walker demo.
subsections.summary: The solver is validated against analytical solutions and state-of-the-art solvers, featuring demo systems like the 'Dr. Legs' bipedal walker.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: PHUMA: Physically Reliable Humanoid Locomotion Dataset
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 196
talks.summary: Presents PHUMA, a large-scale, physically reliable humanoid locomotion dataset. It bridges the gap between small-scale clean data and large-scale noisy data by filtering and retargeting human motion. The dataset enables zero-shot transfer to real hardware with significantly lower tracking error.

subsections.title: Motivation for PHUMA
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison between real-world and simulation data scaling.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights the need for a humanoid locomotion dataset that is both large-scale and physically reliable, as existing datasets often trade one for the other.

subsections.title: Dataset Pipeline
subsections.visual_caption: PHUMA dataset overview with 73 hours of motion.
subsections.summary: The pipeline involves collecting human motions, filtering out physically invalid ones, and retargeting them using physics-aware regularization to create 73 hours of reliable data.

subsections.title: Evaluation & Real-Robot Transfer
subsections.visual_caption: Zero-shot transfer results on a real Unitree G1.
subsections.summary: Policies trained on PHUMA show higher success rates on unseen motions and successful zero-shot transfer to real hardware like the Unitree G1.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: LadderMan: Learning Humanoid Perceptive Ladder Climbing
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 195
talks.summary: Proposes LadderMan, a system for perceptive humanoid ladder climbing and on-ladder manipulation. It uses a two-stage learning pipeline to distill expert policies into a unified vision-based policy. Experiments demonstrate robust climbing on diverse ladders and successful execution of manipulation tasks while maintaining balance.

subsections.title: Motivation & Challenges
subsections.visual_caption: Challenges of ladder climbing for humanoids.
subsections.summary: Ladder climbing is identified as a key milestone for industrial deployment, requiring precise coordination between hands and feet on narrow rungs.

subsections.title: Two-Stage Learning Pipeline
subsections.visual_caption: Method diagram showing policy distillation.
subsections.summary: The system uses hybrid motion tracking to learn expert policies which are then distilled into a single depth-based visual-motor policy using a foundation depth model.

subsections.title: Real-Robot Experiments
subsections.visual_caption: Autonomous ladder climbing and manipulation demo.
subsections.summary: LadderMan demonstrates robust climbing on diverse ladders and performs manipulation tasks like replacing light bulbs while maintaining balance on the ladder.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: TactileStep: Sole Tactile Learning for Regulating Foot--Terrain Interaction in Humanoid Locomotion
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 197
talks.summary: Introduces TactileStep, a method for regulating foot-terrain interaction using sole tactile feedback. It extracts compact features from pressure insoles to provide a sense of touch during locomotion. Real-robot experiments on Unitree G1 show gentler, quieter, and more stable steps across various terrains.

subsections.title: Motivation: Vision vs. Touch
subsections.visual_caption: Hard landing vs. stable support comparison.
subsections.summary: While vision helps plan before contact, touch provides critical information about the actual support available after contact, preventing hard landings.

subsections.title: Tactile Features & Rewards
subsections.visual_caption: Compact tactile features from pressure insoles.
subsections.summary: The method extracts normal force, contact area, and center of pressure as compact features and matches training rewards to different gait phases.

subsections.title: Real-Robot Locomotion Results
subsections.visual_caption: Unitree G1 walking across diverse terrains.
subsections.summary: TactileStep is tested on a real Unitree G1, demonstrating softer, quieter, and more stable landings compared to baselines without tactile feedback.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: OpenHLM: An Empirical Recipe for Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 199
talks.summary: Presents OpenHLM, an empirical recipe for whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation. It utilizes a hierarchical control framework and explores data-efficient training using teleoperation and human-to-humanoid data. The system achieves high success rates on long-horizon tasks and generalizes to outdoor environments.

subsections.title: Motivation & Architecture
subsections.visual_caption: Humanoid using feet and legs for manipulation.
subsections.summary: OpenHLM aims to put the entire humanoid body to work, using a two-level hierarchical control framework for loco-manipulation.

subsections.title: Empirical Recipe for Training
subsections.visual_caption: Empirical recipe for whole-body control.
subsections.summary: The recipe includes joint-space retargeting, robot pre-training transfers, and scaling with cheaper data from stationary teleoperation and human demonstrations.

subsections.title: Long-Horizon Task Demos
subsections.visual_caption: Long-horizon fruit picking and shelf placement demo.
subsections.summary: The system is demonstrated on complex tasks like picking fruits from different heights and placing them on shelves, outperforming baselines in task progress.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: Learning Loco-Manipulation From SMPC Demonstrations With Sparse Offline-to-Online RL
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 201
talks.summary: Describes a method for learning loco-manipulation skills from sampling-based MPC (SMPC) demonstrations. By scaling data collection on GPUs and using sparse offline-to-online RL, it avoids complex reward tuning. The approach enables zero-shot transfer of complex tasks like tire rolling to Spot and G1 robots.

subsections.title: Motivation: Fast Learning from Sparse Rewards
subsections.visual_caption: Training pipeline overview.
subsections.summary: The goal is to learn loco-manipulation skills quickly from sparse rewards, avoiding the time-consuming process of reward tuning.

subsections.title: GPU-Based SMPC Data Collection
subsections.visual_caption: Massively parallel data collection on GPU.
subsections.summary: Data collection is scaled up using sampling-based MPC on GPUs, creating a large offline dataset for reinforcement learning.

subsections.title: Real-Robot Loco-Manipulation
subsections.visual_caption: Spot and G1 performing tire rolling and box pushing.
subsections.summary: Policies transfer zero-shot to real robots, enabling complex tasks like tire rolling and box pushing on Spot and Unitree G1.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: CMP: Robust Whole-Body Tracking for Loco-Manipulation via Competence Manifold Projection
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 202
talks.summary: Introduces Competence Manifold Projection (CMP) for robust whole-body tracking under impossible or out-of-distribution (OOD) commands. It projects infeasible actions onto a learned competence manifold to maximize feasible tracking while maintaining safety. Results show significantly improved survival rates on real legged robots.

subsections.title: Problem: Impossible Commands
subsections.visual_caption: Infeasible command examples (sitting without a chair).
subsections.summary: The talk addresses the problem of robots failing when faced with impossible or out-of-distribution commands, such as being told to sit when no chair is present.

subsections.title: Competence Manifold Projection
subsections.visual_caption: CMP method diagram.
subsections.summary: CMP simplifies the sequential process into a single-step safety test and uses an isomorphic latent space to correct actions toward the policy's competence manifold.

subsections.title: Robust Tracking Results
subsections.visual_caption: Safety comparison in backward pushing task.
subsections.summary: The method significantly improves survival rates under OOD commands, allowing robots to make their best effort safely instead of crashing.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: ResSafe: Learning Safety Filtering with Residual Reinforcement Learning for Humanoids
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 198
talks.summary: Presents ResSafe, a safety filtering method using residual reinforcement learning for humanoids. It decouples safety from performance by learning a residual correction to a frozen reference policy. Hardware deployment on Unitree G1 demonstrates reduced fall rates under perturbations and payloads.

subsections.title: Motivation: Multi-Objective Trade-offs
subsections.visual_caption: Trade-off between performance, safety, and robustness.
subsections.summary: A single RL policy often struggles to balance conflicting objectives like tracking performance and safety under varying payloads.

subsections.title: Residual Safety Filtering
subsections.visual_caption: ResSafe architecture diagram.
subsections.summary: ResSafe learns a residual correction to a frozen reference policy, effectively acting as a learned safety filter without requiring online optimization.

subsections.title: Simulation & Hardware Results
subsections.visual_caption: Unitree G1 robustness tests with payloads.
subsections.summary: The method achieves lower fall rates in simulation and transfers successfully to the Unitree G1 hardware under random payloads.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S7: Humanoid locomotion and whole-body control
talks.title: Humanoid Navigation in Cluttered Environments with a Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Model
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 200
talks.summary: Proposes TANGO, a whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) model for humanoid navigation in cluttered environments. It integrates a navigation foundation model with a diffusion-based action expert and a low-level tracker. The system enables semantic-guided navigation and obstacle avoidance in complex 3D indoor scenes.

subsections.title: Motivation: Cluttered Indoor Navigation
subsections.visual_caption: Navigation challenges in cluttered indoor spaces.
subsections.summary: Existing navigation models are often limited by planar action spaces when dealing with complex 3D spatial obstacles in indoor environments.

subsections.title: TANGO Architecture
subsections.visual_caption: Triple-system whole-body VLA architecture.
subsections.summary: TANGO uses a triple-system architecture combining a navigation foundation model, a diffusion transformer action expert, and a low-level RL tracker.

subsections.title: Experiments & Real-Robot Demo
subsections.visual_caption: Unitree G1 navigating a cluttered room.
subsections.summary: The model achieves state-of-the-art results on navigation benchmarks and is demonstrated on a real Unitree G1 navigating cluttered indoor scenes.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors — A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 97
talks.summary: Introduces VisionSIM, a physically grounded multi-modal simulator for robot perception. It moves beyond idealized sensors by simulating realistic noise, distortions, and artifacts for various modalities like LiDAR, thermal, and event cameras. The platform aims to bridge the sim-to-real gap in perception-heavy tasks.

subsections.title: Motivation and Sensor Fidelity
subsections.visual_caption: Graph showing the trade-off between sensing modalities and simulation fidelity.
subsections.summary: The speaker highlights the critical blind spot in modern simulation platforms regarding how robots actually see the world, particularly for non-conventional modalities.

subsections.title: VisionSIM Overview
subsections.visual_caption: Trade-off between sensor fidelity and supported modalities.
subsections.summary: VisionSIM aims to push the Pareto front by providing high-fidelity simulation across a wide range of sensing modalities, including unconventional ones like thermal and event cameras.

subsections.title: Failure Modes and Dataset Release
subsections.visual_caption: Grid showing various sensor emulation failure modes like ambient light corruption and blur.
subsections.summary: The platform models complex effects like thermal inertia and handprints on tables, and the authors release a large-scale multi-modal indoor dataset.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: MosaicIMU: Composing Carrier Experts for Generalizable Neural Inertial Odometry
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 227
talks.summary: MosaicIMU uses a mixture-of-experts approach to build a generalizable neural inertial odometry model that works across heterogeneous carriers by preserving carrier-specific motion priors.

subsections.title: Problem and Objective
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing different motion priors for various carriers like cars and quadrupeds.
subsections.summary: The talk addresses the challenge of generalizing inertial odometry across different carriers that follow very different motion priors.

subsections.title: MosaicIMU Architecture
subsections.visual_caption: Overall architecture of MosaicIMU featuring a router and expert features.
subsections.summary: The model uses a carrier-conditioned mixture-of-experts where a router composes features at the feature level, fused with a history-aware EKF.

subsections.title: Experiments and Online Adaptation
subsections.visual_caption: Visualization of the dynamic online fine-tuning process on a vehicle dataset.
subsections.summary: MosaicIMU achieves superior performance across carriers and demonstrates effective online adaptation on self-collected vehicle datasets.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: Anchor3R: Streaming 3D Reconstruction with Transient Anchors for Long-Horizon Visual Mapping
talks.affiliation: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 228
talks.summary: Anchor3R enables long-horizon streaming 3D reconstruction by using transient anchors, keeping geometric reasoning local and consistent while bounding GPU memory usage.

subsections.title: Transient Anchors Concept
subsections.visual_caption: Kilometer-scale mapping results using Anchor3R.
subsections.summary: Anchor3R uses the current frame as a transient anchor to reconstruct long routes spanning thousands of images and kilometers.

subsections.title: Pose Reasoning and Optimization
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the loop closure and joint refinement process.
subsections.summary: The network predicts relative poses and local geometry, using overlapping windows and motion averaging to reduce accumulated drift.

subsections.title: System Results and Comparison
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of trajectories between fixed and transient anchors.
subsections.summary: Anchor3R produces smoother local trajectories and more coherent point maps than baselines like LingBot-Map.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: SidewalkBench: Benchmarking Visual Navigation on Urban Sidewalks
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 203
talks.summary: SidewalkBench is a uniform benchmark for evaluating visual navigation on urban sidewalks, featuring procedurally generated and real-world scanned scenes with diverse pedestrian behaviors.

subsections.title: Motivation and Simulation Platform
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of the SidewalkBench simulation platform featuring generated and scanned scenes.
subsections.summary: The speaker introduces the need for a comprehensive benchmark for sidewalk navigation, covering diverse structures, obstacles, and pedestrians.

subsections.title: Evaluation Scenarios
subsections.visual_caption: Grid showing unit-test, pedestrian-reactive, and long-horizon scenarios.
subsections.summary: SidewalkBench includes unit tests for lane following, reactive scenarios for pedestrian interaction, and long-horizon scenarios for real-world mimicry.

subsections.title: Findings and Research Gap
subsections.visual_caption: Bar charts showing failure rates across different scenarios and models.
subsections.summary: Key findings include the importance of sidewalk-specific training data and the significant remaining challenges in pedestrian interaction and long-horizon robustness.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: From Region Arrival to Instance-Level Grounding in Vision-and-Language Navigation
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 205
talks.summary: This work addresses the 'last 3-meter grounding gap' in vision-and-language navigation by introducing REALM, a plug-and-play refinement module that ensures robots actually see and face their target objects.

subsections.title: The Grounding Gap
subsections.visual_caption: Example showing an agent stopping near a target but facing the wrong way.
subsections.summary: The authors argue that conventional success metrics are insufficient if the robot stops near a target but cannot actually see or interact with it.

subsections.title: REALM Refinement Module
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of the REALM pipeline including navigation, refinement, and grounding.
subsections.summary: REALM is a plug-and-play module that adjusts the agent's position and orientation using egocentric RGB to ensure target visibility.

subsections.title: Real-Robot Experiments
subsections.visual_caption: Demo of the Unitree G1 humanoid robot successfully navigating to a target box.
subsections.summary: The method is validated in a real lab environment and on a humanoid robot, demonstrating successful instance-level grounding.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: OSCAR: Obstacle Survival Curves for Adaptive Robot Navigation
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 204
talks.summary: OSCAR learns obstacle survival functions to help robots decide whether to wait for or reroute around obstacles, improving navigation efficiency by estimating optimal patience thresholds.

subsections.title: Adaptive Navigation Problem
subsections.visual_caption: Robot facing a 'Wait or Reroute?' decision at an obstacle.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the inefficiency of static rules for waiting or rerouting when encountering transient versus long-lasting obstacles.

subsections.title: OSCAR Method and Pipeline
subsections.visual_caption: System overview of OSCAR including obstacle detection and decision making.
subsections.summary: OSCAR learns survival functions for different obstacle classes to estimate how long to wait before taking an alternative path.

subsections.title: Simulation and Strategy Comparison
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of different navigation strategies (Always Wait, Always Reroute, OSCAR).
subsections.summary: OSCAR is shown to outperform heuristic baselines in simulation, approaching the performance of an oracle policy with ground truth knowledge.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: TRIAD Planner : Three-Level Robust Imitation Learning for Autonomous Driving
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 226
talks.summary: TRIAD is a robust imitation learning planner for autonomous driving that addresses performance degradation at three levels: ego-state attention, scene understanding, and trajectory selection.

subsections.title: Imitation Learning Challenges
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram explaining why closed-loop imitation performance degrades.
subsections.summary: The talk identifies three key areas where imitation learning can fail: spurious correlations in ego-state, poor scene understanding, and unsafe expert trajectories.

subsections.title: TRIAD Robustness Levels
subsections.visual_caption: Overview of how TRIAD improves robustness at the channel, scene, and decision levels.
subsections.summary: TRIAD constrains ego-state attention and uses an offline VLM to guide attention toward critical agents in the scene.

subsections.title: Risk-Aware Training and Results
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram of risk-aware training using value-at-risk thresholds.
subsections.summary: The planner uses risk-aware training to penalize unsafe trajectories, improving closed-loop performance without additional inference overhead.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: Collaborative Planning for UAV-UGV Teams under Operational Constraints via Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 229
talks.summary: MEND is a neuro-symbolic diffusion framework for collaborative planning of heterogeneous robot teams, enforcing non-differentiable operational constraints like energy and traversability.

subsections.title: Heterogeneous Coordination Challenges
subsections.visual_caption: UAV-UGV team coordination in an environmental monitoring task.
subsections.summary: The speaker discusses the need for robots to satisfy complex constraints like energy limits and recharging requirements during large-scale missions.

subsections.title: MEND Architecture
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture of Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion (MEND).
subsections.summary: MEND uses a masked generator process and logic-induced indicators to enforce constraints during diffusion sampling.

subsections.title: Simulation and Real-World Validation
subsections.visual_caption: Real-world validation with physical UAVs and UGVs.
subsections.summary: The approach is evaluated in high-fidelity simulations and validated with real-world robot teams in a mixed-reality setup.

talks.session_title: Spotlight S8: Perception, navigation and autonomous systems
talks.title: SCoCaT: Success Conditioned Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Spacecraft Docking
talks.poster_info: Poster: Poster Session 3 (Wed 11/11, 10:30 AM–12:00 PM), No. 71
talks.summary: SCoCaT is a constrained reinforcement learning method for spacecraft docking that separates success and survival damping to ensure agents reach the goal safely without hovering indefinitely.

subsections.title: Spacecraft Docking Constraints
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing safety constraints in space missions.
subsections.summary: Safety is critical in space missions, requiring strict adherence to constraints on size, weight, power, and precision.

subsections.title: SCoCaT Method
subsections.visual_caption: Diagram showing the separation of success and survival damping in SCoCaT.
subsections.summary: SCoCaT introduces an additional success critic to bootstrap over early terminations, preventing the agent from hovering near the goal to avoid violations.

subsections.title: Results and Sim-to-Real
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of docking corridor occupancy between CaT and SCoCaT.
subsections.summary: The method shows a significant increase in task completion rates and is successfully transferred from simulation to a physical thruster-equipped platform.

talks.session_title: Keynote III — Fei-Fei Li
talks.title: Atlas: A Unified World Model for Generation and Reconstruction
talks.summary: Fei-Fei Li introduces Atlas, a unified world model designed for both high-fidelity generation and precise 3D reconstruction. The model uses an autoregressive transformer architecture to predict future viewpoints, enabling applications in robotics simulation, real-to-sim transfer, and creative content generation.
talks.official_abstract: Presenting recent advances in spatial intelligence and world modeling by the research team at World Labs, featuring Atlas, an autoregressive frame generation foundation model that unifies pixel generation and 3D scene reconstruction.
talks.speaker_bio: Fei-Fei Li is the inaugural Sequoia Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University, Founding Co-Director of Stanford HAI, and Founder & CEO of World Labs.

subsections.title: Introduction and Robotics Motivation
subsections.visual_caption: Robot arm holding a marble with the question 'What should the robot do next?'
subsections.summary: The talk begins by framing the fundamental challenge of robotics: determining the next action based on the state of the world and a specific goal.

subsections.title: Defining World Models: Rendering, Planning, and Simulating
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of rendering, planning, and simulating in world models.
subsections.summary: Fei-Fei Li explains how world models unify the problems of understanding environments (rendering), predicting consequences (planning), and simulating states.

subsections.title: Atlas Architecture: Autoregressive Foundation Model
subsections.visual_caption: Architecture diagram of Atlas as a multimodal autoregressive foundation model.
subsections.summary: Atlas is introduced as a multimodal autoregressive transformer trained from scratch to handle text, images, video, depth, and 3D structure inputs.

subsections.title: Unifying Generation and Reconstruction
subsections.visual_caption: Comparison of dense reconstruction, sparse reconstruction, and pure generation.
subsections.summary: The speaker demonstrates how Atlas can scale from dense 3D reconstruction with many views to zero-shot generation from a single text prompt.

subsections.title: Technical Insight: Viewpoint Prediction
subsections.visual_caption: Slide titled 'Viewpoint is all you need' showing camera conditioning.
subsections.summary: The core technical insight of Atlas is that predicting the next viewpoint through strong camera conditioning is the key objective function for world modeling.

subsections.title: Quantitative Benchmarks and Performance
subsections.visual_caption: Benchmark scores showing Atlas ranking #1 on Rapidata's Camera Movement Benchmark.
subsections.summary: Atlas is shown to outperform state-of-the-art video models and specialized 3D reconstruction methods across multiple datasets and metrics.

subsections.title: Applications: Simulation, Navigation, and Real-to-Sim
subsections.visual_caption: Robots trained in virtual worlds and deployed zero-shot in the real world.
subsections.summary: The presentation highlights practical applications, including real-time generation at 15 FPS and zero-shot deployment of robots trained entirely in Atlas-generated simulations.

subsections.title: BEHAVIOR Challenge and Lab Contributions
subsections.visual_caption: Announcement of the 2nd BEHAVIOR Challenge at CoRL 2026.
subsections.summary: The talk concludes with the announcement of the BEHAVIOR challenge winners and a summary of papers contributed by the Stanford Vision and Learning Lab.

subsections.title: BEHAVIOR Challenge and Stanford Lab Papers
subsections.visual_caption: Slide listing 26 papers from the Stanford Vision and Learning Lab at CoRL.
subsections.summary: Fei-Fei Li highlights the 2nd BEHAVIOR Challenge and the significant contribution of her lab to the CoRL conference with 26 papers.

talks.session_title: Fireside Chat — Lisa Su & Fei-Fei Li
talks.title: Fireside Chat with Lisa Su and Fei-Fei Li
talks.summary: A fireside chat featuring AMD CEO Lisa Su and Fei-Fei Li, moderated by Peter Stone, discussing the intersection of high-performance computing and physical AI. They explore AMD's strategy in robotics, the acquisition of World Labs, the future of world models, and the critical need for public sector compute resources.
talks.official_abstract: Presenting recent advances in spatial intelligence and world modeling by the research team at World Labs, featuring Atlas, an autoregressive frame generation foundation model that unifies pixel generation and 3D scene reconstruction.
talks.speaker_bio: Fei-Fei Li is the inaugural Sequoia Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University, Founding Co-Director of Stanford HAI, and Founder & CEO of World Labs.

subsections.title: Introduction of Lisa Su
subsections.visual_caption: Title slide for the Fireside Chat with Lisa Su.
subsections.summary: Session chair Yuke Zhu introduces Dr. Lisa Su, Chair and CEO of AMD, highlighting her leadership in the semiconductor industry and AMD's role in the AI revolution.

subsections.title: AMD's Strategy for Physical AI and Robotics
subsections.visual_caption: Peter Stone, Lisa Su, and Fei-Fei Li seated on stage for the chat.
subsections.summary: Lisa Su discusses AMD's investment across the AI stack and the massive opportunity in physical AI and robotics, which requires a deep understanding of physics and environment models.

subsections.title: Scaling World Models with Advanced Compute
subsections.visual_caption: Fei-Fei Li discussing the vision for world models.
subsections.summary: Fei-Fei Li explains how joining AMD expands World Labs' capabilities to build large-scale world models, emphasizing the fundamental link between computing power and AI intelligence.

subsections.title: Hardware-Software Co-optimization for Robotics
subsections.visual_caption: Lisa Su discussing compute demands in robotics.
subsections.summary: The panelists discuss the unique systems challenges in robotics, including the need for low-latency, power-efficient compute at the edge and the importance of hardware-software co-design.

subsections.title: Public Sector Compute Access and NAIRR
subsections.visual_caption: Fei-Fei Li speaking about the need for public sector compute resources.
subsections.summary: Fei-Fei Li advocates for the National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) bill, arguing that public sector access to compute is vital for innovation, student training, and responsible AI development.

subsections.title: Slido Q&A: AMD Robotics Team and PhD Career Paths
subsections.visual_caption: Peter Stone reading audience questions from a tablet.
subsections.summary: Lisa Su confirms AMD's commitment to robotics research and both speakers offer advice on the enduring value of a PhD for developing deep intuition and solving the hardest problems.

subsections.title: Human Intelligence vs. AI and Closing Advice
subsections.visual_caption: Wide shot of the panel during the final discussion.
subsections.summary: The chat concludes with a discussion on the efficiency of the human brain versus AI models and final words of encouragement for students to be ambitious and honest in their research.

talks.session_title: Special Panel Debate
talks.title: CoRL 2026 Special Debate: Will Behavior Cloning + In-Domain Fine-Tuning Lead to Commercially Viable Generalist Robots?
talks.affiliation: Google DeepMind, TU Berlin, Stanford, MIT, MIT, Imperial College London, CMU
talks.summary: This is the second half of a formal debate regarding the future of generalist robotics. Panelists discuss the viability of behavior cloning and fine-tuning versus simulation and zero-shot generalization, touching on safety-critical systems, throughput metrics, and the distinction between fast reactive control (System 1) and slow reasoning (System 2).

subsections.title: Introduction and Proposition
subsections.visual_caption: The proposition slide defining the debate topic.
subsections.summary: Vincent Vanhoucke introduces the panel and the core proposition: that the current recipe of behavior cloning, pre-training, and in-domain fine-tuning will lead to commercially viable generalist robots.

subsections.title: Pro Side Opening Statement: Chelsea Finn
subsections.visual_caption: Chelsea Finn presenting the Pro side's opening arguments.
subsections.summary: Chelsea Finn argues that high reliability is the key to commercial viability and that large-scale data and in-domain fine-tuning are the essential ingredients to achieve it.

subsections.title: Con Side Opening Statement: Leslie Kaelbling
subsections.visual_caption: Leslie Kaelbling presenting the Con side's opening arguments.
subsections.summary: Leslie Kaelbling argues that the current recipe is becoming overly complicated and that we need a more heterogeneous architecture rather than a single 'true' trick.

subsections.title: Pro Side Rebuttal: Pulkit Agrawal
subsections.visual_caption: Pulkit Agrawal presenting the Pro side's rebuttal.
subsections.summary: Pulkit Agrawal argues that commercial viability is achievable by focusing on specific industrial applications, such as pick-and-place, and that performance is the missing link.

subsections.title: Con Side Rebuttal: Edward Johns
subsections.visual_caption: Edward Johns presenting the Con side's rebuttal.
subsections.summary: Edward Johns argues that the current data-driven approach is too expensive and that we need to focus on meaning and exploration rather than just imitation.

subsections.title: Panel Debate and Closing
subsections.visual_caption: The panel members engaging in a lively debate.
subsections.summary: The panelists debate the role of simulation, the definition of generalist robots, and the path forward for commercial viability.

subsections.title: Rebuttals: Simulation and Solution Spaces
subsections.visual_caption: Panelists Edward Johns and Yonatan Bisk debating on stage.
subsections.summary: Panelists argue about the necessity of simulation to avoid the high cost of human data collection and the difficulty of fully characterizing solution spaces for safety-critical systems.

subsections.title: Open Debate: Zero-Shot vs. Fine-Tuning
subsections.visual_caption: Pulkit Agrawal explaining throughput as a metric for commercial viability.
subsections.summary: The discussion shifts to whether zero-shot generalization is a realistic goal or if fine-tuning is an inherent part of creating expert systems, with a focus on throughput as the primary commercial metric.

subsections.title: The Barista Analogy and Expert Training
subsections.visual_caption: Chelsea Finn discussing the training requirements for a barista.
subsections.summary: Chelsea Finn uses the example of training a barista to illustrate that even humans require significant in-domain practice to reach expert-level reliability and throughput.

subsections.title: System 1 and System 2 in Robotics
subsections.visual_caption: Leslie Kaelbling discussing time-sensitive reasoning.
subsections.summary: Panelists debate the interaction between reactive control and high-level reasoning, emphasizing that commercial systems must respond in a time-sensitive manner.

subsections.title: Closing Audience Poll
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing the debate thesis for the final audience poll.
subsections.summary: The moderator calls for a final audience vote to see if opinions shifted during the debate.

talks.session_title: Closing Musical Interlude
talks.title: String Quartet Performance
talks.summary: A musical interlude featuring a string quartet led by robotics researcher Peter Stone. The quartet performs movements from Dvorak's American String Quartet and 'Spider Dreams' by the Turtle Island String Quartet.

subsections.title: Dvorak: American String Quartet
subsections.visual_caption: String quartet performing on stage.
subsections.summary: The quartet performs the final movement of Dvorak's American String Quartet.

subsections.title: Musician Introductions
subsections.visual_caption: Peter Stone introducing the members of the quartet.
subsections.summary: Peter Stone introduces the professional musicians and researchers making up the quartet.

subsections.title: Turtle Island String Quartet: Spider Dreams
subsections.visual_caption: Quartet performing a jazz-influenced piece.
subsections.summary: The quartet performs 'Spider Dreams', a more contemporary, jazz-influenced piece.

talks.session_title: Awards Ceremony & Farewell
talks.title: CoRL 2026 Awards Ceremony, Best Paper Announcements & Closing Remarks
talks.summary: Yuke Zhu provides a summary of the conference, sharing highlights, social media feedback, and a humorous 'Human vs PowerPoint' debugging moment. He acknowledges the massive growth of the conference and thanks the entire organizing committee, area chairs, volunteers, and sponsors for their contributions.

subsections.title: Awards Introduction
subsections.visual_caption: Vincent Vanhoucke at the podium for the awards ceremony.
subsections.summary: Vincent Vanhoucke begins the awards presentation, reflecting on the conference and the mentorship he received from Peter Stone.

subsections.title: Conference Highlights & Feedback
subsections.visual_caption: Photo montage of conference highlights and social media feedback.
subsections.summary: Yuke Zhu reviews the conference's success, showing a photo montage and positive social media reactions from attendees.

subsections.title: Organizing Committee Recognition
subsections.visual_caption: Slide listing the CoRL 2026 Organizing Committee members.
subsections.summary: The general chairs and program chairs are thanked for their extensive preparation work over the past two years.

subsections.title: Area Chairs & Robot Learning Foundation
subsections.visual_caption: Slide showing the Robot Learning Foundation board of directors.
subsections.summary: Recognition is given to the senior area chairs, area chairs, and the Robot Learning Foundation for managing the review process.

subsections.title: Award Selection Process
subsections.visual_caption: Slide detailing the award selection criteria and process.
subsections.summary: Katerina Fragkiadaki explains the rigorous process used to select finalists and winners from the 21 long-oral papers.

subsections.title: Best Student Paper Award
subsections.visual_caption: Winner slide for Best Student Paper: RoboTTT.
subsections.summary: The Best Student Paper Award is presented to 'RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies' by Yunfan Jiang et al.

subsections.title: Best Conference Paper Award
subsections.visual_caption: Winner slide for Best Conference Paper: SuperMimic.
subsections.summary: The Best Conference Paper Award is presented to 'SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model' by Qiayuan Liao et al.

subsections.visual_caption: Slide thanking General Chair Yuke Zhu and OpenReview Chair Carlo Sferrazza.
subsections.summary: Ani Majumdar and Dieter Fox thank the general chairs and the OpenReview chair for their tireless work behind the scenes.

subsections.visual_caption: Slide announcing the IEEE Transactions on Robot Learning.
